tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )

schema.name: Workflow
schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

## A.4 Problèmes trouvés

- **P1 — lecture littérale des opérations dérivées sur la vue** (brief A1 ; WC4 C2, C3).
  - Passage du brief : « réalisées par les opérations dérivées de `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` sur `s.view c` ».
  - Exemple : S3, pas 8. Avec `Arena.IssueD` sur `a10.view 0`, `store` est rejeté (`S3_8_view_literal`), alors que le corpus prescrit `ok`.
  - Choix fait : la convention du jalon 1, tirée de WC4 C3. Il faut confirmer qu'il est le bon.
- **P2 — S10 : désaccord entre le corpus et le modèle.**
  - **Clause citée par le corpus :** O4.7, avec la justification « `g` détenue par `f0`, son anchor effectif `root_T` passe en `f1` ».
  - **État :** `r3`. Depuis `MX₃`, `c0` a acquis `g` (autorité 4, tenue par la frame 0) puis est entré en `f1` en cédant `m := derive(root_M, Modify)`, avec un local `M′`.
  - **Verdict effectif :** `ok` de la machine avec la bibliothèque, pas seulement du noyau. `S10_1_ok` (`S10.lean:43`) établit que `transfer(M, M′)` est `ok` et admis par `Encap` ; `s10_trace` (`:52`) en fait une `EncapsulatedTrace` depuis l'état initial. Après le pas, l'ancre effective de `g` est en `f1`, qui n'est pas ancêtre de la frame 0 (`¬ EffAnchorOKC r4 4 (some 0)`), et `exitFrameC(f1)` est rejeté.
  - **Cause :** la première phrase de §63.7 porte sur les autorités tenues **déplacées** (« All moved held authorities … satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` »). `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) ne porte que sur les autorités tenues par des places. `g` est tenue par une frame et ne bouge pas. Les autorités déplacées (`guarded` vers `slot′`, `root_T` vers `M′`) satisfont la règle en `f1`. La seconde phrase, « no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred », ne dit pas si elle couvre une autorité non déplacée dont l'ancre effective est déplacée. Le modèle de la Spec 1 encode §63.7 de la même façon (`Access/Ops.lean`, `TransferPre.anchorOrderHeld` : les seules autorités `AnchorMoves`).
  - **Conséquence :** le pas n'est pas dangereux. L'état est bloqué : `f1` ne peut plus sortir. C'est un silence de la Spec 1 §63.7, à arbitrer ; ni le corpus ni le modèle ne sont corrigés.
- **P3 — S11 : mise en place sous-spécifiée.**
  - Passage : « `c1 : enterFrame f1′` ; `acquire(e)` → `g` détenue par `f1′` ».
  - Exemple : `f1′` entrée sans paramètre ne tient aucune autorité sur `lock`. C14.3 (`CtrlRight`) échoue, et `acquire` n'est pas habilité (`S11_setup_wait`).
  - Les cas S11 sont encodés en cédant `o1′ := derive(o1, Observe)` à `f1′`. Les verdicts du corpus sont alors tous obtenus. Ce choix de mise en place est à confirmer.
- **P4 — S12 « déjà encodé ».** Aucun théorème des jalons 1–2 n'encodait `write3(lock)`. Le jalon 2 le mentionne seulement dans son rapport. Encodé ici : `S12_1_ok`, `S12_2_ok`.
- **P5 — jumeau de S17a.** Le jalon 1 encodait `endUse(M)`, positif de S17b, faute du positif littéral (remarque X2 de `spec2-m1-close.md`). Le jumeau du corpus, `endUse(slot)` puis `endUse(lock)` admis par `Encap`, est encodé ici (`S17a_2_ok`).
- **P6 — clause de rejet du `reset` sous bloc actif.** Le corpus cite §78.2. L'opération dérivée rejette au `derive` de `internal` : son mode effectif sur `R1` est absent (§43.3, §60.2). Même verdict. Sur les états accessibles séquentiels, `Arena.reset_iff_derive_release` établit l'équivalence des deux lectures. Elle n'est pas transportée au cas concurrent.
- **P7 — `reject` des opérations à issue `ok` seule.** `UnlockOk` et `ResetLockOk` ne définissent que `ok` (WC4 C17, C18 ne donnent pas d'autre issue). Le modèle ne distingue donc pas `reject` de « non habilité » pour elles. S11.3 et S15.4 sont encodés par l'absence d'`ok` et la clause défaillante du corpus.
- **P8 — W-C22.2 : désaccord sur « `acquire(e)` plus jamais habilitée ».**
  - **Clause citée par le corpus :** C13.9/C14 (« descendant bloquant »).
  - **État :** `x5`, après le `deriveSync` brut du contexte 1 depuis `MX₄` ; le registre garde `grant = none`.
  - **Verdict effectif :** dans `x5`, `acquire` n'est habilité pour aucun contexte (`W_C22_2_encap`). Mais le contexte 1 peut libérer la dérivée par un `release` ordinaire (O3), pas `ok` admis par `Encap` ; `GrantDiscipline` est alors rétablie et `acquire(e)` par le contexte 1 est habilité (`W_C22_2_reenable`, `MX.lean:365`). WC4 C15 (effet) le permet : la dérivée « is ordinary after creation … for its … legal release ».
  - **Lecture :** « plus jamais » est trop fort : dans ce cas, le blocage cesse au `release` de la dérivée. Aucun énoncé général sur la durée du blocage n'est prouvé. Ni le corpus ni le modèle ne sont corrigés.

## A.5 Décisions de représentation du jalon 3

1. **État de bibliothèque.** `SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg`. `Encap` garde sa signature et est lu sur `(st.1, st.2.1)`.
2. **Opérations d'arène exécutées par un contexte.** `newArena` : clauses de `NewArenaBase` sur la vue, §76.6 sur l'état concurrent. `issue` : forme d'`IssueD` avec `opStepC` pour `split` et `store`. `reset` : `ResetD` sur la vue. Voir P1.
3. **Issues.** Les relations d'arène ont des issues `Outcome3`, `fail` compris pour `issue`. `LStep` ne contient que les pas `ok`, comme au jalon 1.
4. **`ArenaInvC`** est `Arena.LInv` sur `s.flat` : `ArenaInv` (§55), avec `IssuedShape` et la borne des `internal`.
5. **`AdminSep`.** Partie inter-registres de §56, invariant de trace. L'unicité intra-registre n'est énoncée que pour le registre de synchronisation (`SyncInv.unique`, jalon 1).
6. **`lstep_preserves`.** `AdminSep` y est une hypothèse conditionnelle, active pour `issue` et `reset` seulement.
7. **`realize` et `StepOblC`.** Ils prennent le registre d'arènes. `issue` est réalisé par `store` sur l'état après `split`, comme `RefinementArena.kexp`. `newArena` et `reset` n'ont aucune opération brute.
8. **Corpus.** Contrat `KC sm` ; encodages des verdicts de § A.3 ; noms `S<cas>_<n>_<verdict>`. Le verdict obtenu est dans le nom quand il diffère du corpus (S10), et le désaccord est dans la docstring.
9. **§76.6, « `WF3` ».** Lu `WF3 s.flat`, composant de la Spec 1 sur les frames vivantes. `FramesC`, la structure des contextes de WC4 C20, n'est pas exigé par `newArena`, qui ne change pas les contextes ; il tient sur les états atteints (T2).

## A.6 Écarts avec la Spec 1

Aucun, hors la réindexation sur `ancestorC` exigée par WC4 C3. A5 montre qu'en contexte unique les opérations d'arène coïncident avec celles d'`Arena.lean`, issue par issue, et que leurs réalisations coïncident avec celles de `RefinementArena.lean`.

# Corpus adversarial — ERN Spec 2, jalon 3 (v3)

**v3** — ajout des témoins de passation (§ 2 bis) ; aucun verdict de la v2 n'est modifié. **v2** — corrections après le rapport `spec2-m3.md` et sa revue ; chaque changement est listé en § 5. Les verdicts corrigés le sont depuis la Spec 1 et WC4, pas depuis le modèle.

Document de travail, non normatif, joint au brief du jalon 3. Dérivé des règles de la Spec 1 v0.1 et de WC4 corrigée ; aucun verdict ne vient du modèle Lean. Chaque rejet a un jumeau positif. Les cas sont des traces de pas abstraits, sans syntaxe.

## 0. Conventions

- `c0` : contexte initial, frame de base `f0` ; `fk` : frames entrées par `enterFrame` ; `c1`, `c2` : contextes créés par `spawn`.
- `root_X` : autorité racine `Modify` de la place `X`, détenue par son owner (§40, `RootHeld`).
- **Verdicts** : `ok` ; `reject` ; `fail` (seulement `alloc` et `issue`, §58, §77.4) ; `non habilité` (aucune issue : attente, WC4 C8, C16) ; `ok noyau / hors C22` (pas `ok` de la machine, refusé par `Encap`, WC4 C22–C23) ; `hors fragment` (dépend d'OB-C01 à OB-C06).
- **`reject` / `non habilité`** (critère P7, à arbitrer) : une clause de **synchronisation** défaillante (contrôleur occupé C16, `grant ≠ none` C14.2) rend l'opération `non habilitée` ; une clause d'**autorité ou de registre** défaillante (C17.2, C18.1, toute clause de la Spec 1) donne `reject`. La durée ne joue pas : un `reject` peut cesser (S11.3 après `join`), un `non habilité` peut durer (S11.2). WC4 C17/C18 ne définissent que `ok` : leur `reject` est encodé par l'absence d'issue `ok` plus la clause défaillante.
- Les réalisations mémoire (jalon 2) ne sont pas répétées. Chaque pas `ok` d'un cas est **éligible** à une réalisation sous les paramètres (`ParamsOK`) et les obligations par pas (`StepOblC`) du jalon 2 ; l'acceptation abstraite n'établit pas ces obligations.

Puis `c0 : write3(Y)` via `root_Y` → `reject` (§43.3 : descendant `Modify` actif) | Négatif : S1a (même construction, `Y` local de `f1`) |

import Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.MX

/-!
# Corpus of milestone 3, case S10

`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10: from `MX₃`, context 0 acquires the grant `g` (held by frame 0), enters
`f1` yielding `m := derive(root_M, Modify)` with a local `M′` of the shape of `M`, and in `f1`
transfers `M` into `M′`. Verdicts of the corpus: `ok` (§63.7 constrains only the moved held
authorities, and `AnchorOrderHeld`, §44, only authorities held by places; `g`, held by frame 0 and
not moved, is constrained by no clause); then `exitFrameC(f1)` `reject` (§73.4); then
`transfer(M′, M)` `ok` (§63.3); then `exitFrameC(f1)` `ok`: a liveness trap, reversible. The
sequential counterpart, in the kernel of Spec 1 alone, is `Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.S10Seq`.
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency.Corpus

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.Concurrency
open Ern.Concurrency.Traces (L0)

/-- `c0 : acquire(e)` in `MX₃`: `g`, authority 4, held by frame 0 (WC4 C16). -/
def r1 : SC := deriveSyncEff x2 0 3
/-- `m := derive(root_M, Modify, footprint(M))`, authority 5 (O1). -/
def r2 : SC := r1.set (deriveEff (r1.view 0) 0 [1, 2] .modify)
/-- `enterFrame f1` yielding `m`, with the local `M′` (place 7, fields 8 and 9, `Uninit`) (O6). -/
def r3 : SC := enterEffC r2 0 [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]
/-- `f1 : transfer(M, M′)` (O4). -/
def r4 : SC := transferEffC r3 0 0 7

/-- The setup of S10 (`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10): `acquire(e)` by context 0, `derive`, then
`enterFrame f1` yielding `m` with the local `M′`. -/
theorem s10_setup : AcquireOk KM L0 x2 regX 0 0 (r1, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) ∧
    opStepC KM (.derive 0 [1, 2] .modify) 0 r1 (.ok r2) ∧
    opStepC KM (.enter [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]) 0 r2 (.ok r3) :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, ⟨3, none⟩, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩,
    ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩⟩

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10, step 1, `ok`, then `exitFrameC(f1)` `reject` (§73.4): in `f1`,
`transfer(M, M′)` by context 0 is an `ok` step of Spec 1 §63 re-indexed admitted by `Encap`; after
it, the effective anchor of `g` (authority 4) is in frame 1, which is not an ancestor of frame 0
holding `g` (`EffAnchorOKC` fails for `g` and its holder frame), and `exitFrameC(f1)` is rejected.
The positive twin (`M′` local of `f0`) is `Ern.Concurrency.EncapTraces.traceB`. -/
theorem S10_1_ok : opStepC KM (.transfer 0 7) 0 r3 (.ok r4) ∧
    Encap L0 (r3, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) (.kernel 0 (.transfer 0 7)) ∧
    ¬ EffAnchorOKC r4 4 (some 0) ∧ opStepC KM .exit 0 r4 .reject :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, (by decide : TransferExcl L0 (r3, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) 0), by decide,
    ⟨by decide, .reject (by decide)⟩⟩

/-- The steps of S10 form an `EncapsulatedTrace` from the initial state (WC4 C22, C23): the
effective verdict of `S10_1_ok` is an `ok` of the machine with the library, not only of the
kernel. -/
theorem s10_trace : EncapsulatedTrace KM L0 (x0, [], [])
    [.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 1), .newMutex 0 3, .acquire 0 0,
     .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .modify),
     .kernel 0 (.enter [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]),
     .kernel 0 (.transfer 0 7)] (r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩], []) := by
  have h := mx3_trace.snoc (lbl := .acquire 0 0) (st' := (r1, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) trivial
    (.acquire s10_setup.1)
  have h := h.snoc (lbl := .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .modify))
    (st' := (r2, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) (by decide : ∀ e ∈ ([⟨3, some 4⟩] : SyncReg), e.Live r1 →
      0 ≠ e.guarded) (.kernel s10_setup.2.1)
  have h := h.snoc (lbl := .kernel 0 (.enter [5] [(none, 0), (some 7, 0), (some 7, 0)]))
    (st' := (r3, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) trivial (.kernel s10_setup.2.2)
  exact h.snoc (lbl := .kernel 0 (.transfer 0 7)) (st' := (r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩], [])) S10_1_ok.2.1
    (.kernel S10_1_ok.1)

/-- `f1 : transfer(M′, M)` (O4). -/
def r5 : SC := transferEffC r4 0 7 0
/-- `exitFrameC(f1)` (O7, WC4 C6). -/
def r6 : SC := exitEffC r5 0

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10, suite, `ok` (§63.3: the leaves of `M` are `Moved`, not `Init`;
§63.1 via `m` and `root_M′`): `transfer(M′, M)` from `f1`, admitted by `Encap`. -/
theorem S10_2_ok : opStepC KM (.transfer 7 0) 0 r4 (.ok r5) ∧
    Encap L0 (r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) (.kernel 0 (.transfer 7 0)) :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, (by decide : TransferExcl L0 (r4, [⟨3, some 4⟩]) 7)⟩

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S10, suite, `ok` (§73.4, §73.5): `exitFrameC(f1)` after the transfer
back. -/
theorem S10_3_ok : opStepC KM .exit 0 r5 (.ok r6) := ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩

end Ern.Concurrency.Corpus

  ⟨⟨by decide, ⟨3, none⟩, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩,
    ⟨by decide, ⟨3, some 4⟩, 4, rfl, by decide, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩⟩

/-! ## W-C22.2 (`corpus-spec2-m3.md` §2) -/

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §2 W-C22.2, `ok noyau / hors C22.2`: from `MX₄`, context 1 outside
`acquire` takes the raw `deriveSync(guarded)` step under the library instantiation (the facts
C14.1–C14.3 hold); `Encap` excludes it (WC4 C22.2). After the step the registry still records
`grant = none` while an active descendant covers `T`: `GrantDiscipline` fails, and `acquire(e)` is
enabled for neither context while the derivative is active (WC4 C13.9, C14: blocking
descendant); it is enabled again after its ordinary `release` (`W_C22_2_reenable`). Positive twin:
`S2_1_ok`. -/
theorem W_C22_2_encap : DeriveSyncStep (libKC KM L0) regX x4 1 3 (.ok x5) ∧
    ¬ Encap L0 (x4, regX) (.deriveSync 1 3) ∧ ¬ GrantDiscipline x5 regX ∧
    ∀ st', ¬ AcquireOk KM L0 x5 regX 0 0 st' ∧ ¬ AcquireOk KM L0 x5 regX 1 0 st' := by
  refine ⟨⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, fun h => h ⟨3, none⟩ (by decide) (by decide) rfl,
    fun h => (by decide : ¬ NoCoveringDesc x5 3) (h ⟨3, none⟩ (by decide) (by decide) rfl),
    fun st' => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨-, e, he, -, hpre, -⟩
    cases he; exact (by decide : ¬ DeriveSyncPre (libKC KM L0) regX x5 0 3) hpre
  · rintro ⟨-, e, he, -, hpre, -⟩
    cases he; exact (by decide : ¬ DeriveSyncPre (libKC KM L0) regX x5 1 3) hpre

/-- `c1 : release(g)` of the raw grant of W-C22.2 (O3). -/
def x5r : SC := x5.set (releaseEff (x5.view 1) 5)

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §2 W-C22.2, `acquire(e)` "de nouveau habilitée après son `release`
ordinaire": after the raw `deriveSync` of `W_C22_2_encap`, context 1 releases the derivative by an
ordinary `release` (O3), an `ok` step that `Encap` admits (WC4 C15 effect: the derivative "is
ordinary after creation … for its … legal release"); `GrantDiscipline` holds again and
`acquire(e)` by context 1 is enabled. -/
theorem W_C22_2_reenable : opStepC KM (.release 5) 1 x5 (.ok x5r) ∧
    Encap L0 (x5, regX) (.kernel 1 (.release 5)) ∧ GrantDiscipline x5r regX ∧

/-- `ArenaReg.unique` (Spec 1 §56, first sentence: "An authority identity may serve as `internal`
for at most one live administrative abstraction"), inside the arena registry: two live entries,
by position, do not share their `internal` identity. -/
def ArenaReg.unique (ar : ArenaReg) (s : SC) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i j : Nat) (E E' : Arena.ArenaEntry), ar[i]? = some E → ar[j]? = some E' →
    Arena.Live s.flat E → Arena.Live s.flat E' → E.internal = E'.internal → i = j

theorem append_one_cases {ar : ArenaReg} {E₀ E : Arena.ArenaEntry} {j : Nat}

  by_cases hj : j < ar.length

  · rw [List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_of_not_lt hj)] at h
    cases e : j - ar.length with

the `internal` at every position. -/

import Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.AR
import Ern.Concurrency.RealizeSound

/-!
# Corpus of milestone 3: the arena run of S3 in the memory machine

The trace of block AR and of `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S3 up to step 3 (`c1 : acquire(e2)`, then
`issue(arena, R1, d1)` under `g2`) as a translated run (`SimRunC`), on the pattern of
`Ern.Concurrency.RealizeWitness.s4_realized`: under parameters fixed once from the final places,
every step satisfies its obligations (`StepOblC`), the run is realized by an execution of `ok` raw
steps from the empty memory state, none `ub`, with `ReprC` at each state (Spec 1 §77, §82; WC4
C19). At the state before `issue`, the hypotheses of `issue_pointer_soundC` hold jointly, and the
reference written into `d1` decodes to the address of the issued region (Spec 1 §82.3).

Contexts interleave at the grain of abstract steps, as everywhere in `Ern.Concurrency.Realize`.
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.ARRealize

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement
open Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement.Runs Ern.Concurrency Ern.Concurrency.Corpus
open Ern.Concurrency.Traces (L0)

/-- Parameters of the run, fixed once from its final places (Spec 1 §82): the test layout,
geometry and reference encoding of `Refinement.Runs`. -/
def πA : Refinement.Params Unit := piOf a8.P []

/-- The memory state realizing the initial state of block AR (Spec 1 §47, `repr_init`). -/
def mA0 : Machine.State :=
  run Machine.State.empty (initOps πA.pl πA.geom πA.rtok πA.L πA.ty πA.ival arst)

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` §1 S3 up to step 3, in the memory machine (Spec 1 §77, §82; WC4 C19, C25),
at the grain of abstract steps: the run is realized by an execution of `ok` raw steps from the empty
memory state, none `ub`; it is an `EncapsulatedTrace` from the initial state of Spec 1 §47; `ReprC`
holds at every state of the run. -/
theorem s3_realized :
    ((∃ ops, Machine.Exec (· = ·) obR obW ops Machine.State.empty mA10) ∧
      ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a8 mA10 ∧
      ∃ lbls, EncapsulatedTrace KA L0 (SC.ofS3 (S3.init arst), [], []) lbls (a8, regA8, arA1)) ∧
    (∃ ops, Machine.Exec (· = ·) obR obW ops Machine.State.empty mA10 ∧
      Along (NoUB (· = ·) obR obW) Machine.State.empty ops) ∧
    ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a0 mA0 ∧ ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a1 mA1 ∧ ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a2 mA2 ∧
    ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a2 mA3 ∧ ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a3 mA4 ∧ ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a4 mA5 ∧
    ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a4 mA6 ∧ ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a5 mA7 ∧ ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a6 mA8 ∧
    ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a7 mA9 := by
  have hdd := ddKC [2]
  have hπ := piOf_ok a8.P []
  exact ⟨simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim10, concrete_safety hdd hπ ar_sim10,
    (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim0).2.1, (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim1).2.1,
    (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim2).2.1, (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim3).2.1,
    (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim4).2.1, (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim5).2.1,
    (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim6).2.1, (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim7).2.1,
    (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim8).2.1, (simulationC hdd hπ ar_sim9).2.1⟩

/-- The state after `split` of `internal` on `R1` by context 1 (Spec 1 §61). -/
def tA : S3 := splitEff (a7.view 1) 4 [[5]]

/-- The address of the issued block, read on `tA` (Spec 1 §82.2, `ptrAddr`). -/
def adA : Nat := ptrAddr mA9 πA.L tA a7.A.length

/-- The hypotheses of `issue_pointer_soundC` hold jointly at the state before `issue` (Spec 1
§82.3; WC4 C25): `ReprC` (from the run), `FramesC`, `WF3` and `NoDangling` (from
`encapsulated_inv` on the run's trace), the `ok` issue `S3_3_ok`, the entry of the arena, a
destination leaf of pointer size, and the obligation of the encoding for the reference. -/
theorem s3_issue_hyps : ReprC πA.L πA.rtok a7 mA9 ∧ FramesC a7 ∧ WF3 a7.flat ∧
    NoDangling a7.flat ∧ IssueStepC KA a7 arA 1 0 [5] 8 (.ok (a8, arA1)) ∧
    arA[0]? = some ⟨4, 4, [5, 6], []⟩ ∧ (πA.L 8).len = πA.pe.size ∧
    PtrEncAt πA.pe adA (some (anchorAlloc πA.L tA a7.A.length)) := by
  obtain ⟨-, hR, lbls, htr⟩ := simulationC (ddKC [2]) (piOf_ok a8.P []) ar_sim9
  obtain ⟨hk, -, -⟩ := encapsulated_inv (ddKC [2]) arst_ok htr
  exact ⟨hR, hk.1.1, hk.1.2, hk.2.1.2.2, S3_3_ok, rfl, by decide, by decide, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- `issue_pointer_soundC` on the run (Spec 1 §82.3, §77): after the realization of
`issue(arena, R1, d1)`, the bytes of `d1` decode to the address `adA` of the issued region, every
byte carries the provenance of the allocation of the effective anchor of the block, and that
address is 48 under the test parameters. -/
theorem s3_issue_pointer : πA.pe.decode (bytesOf mA10 πA.L 8) = adA ∧
    (∀ i, i < (πA.L 8).len → (bytesOf mA10 πA.L 8 i).2 = some (anchorAlloc πA.L tA a7.A.length)) ∧
    adA = 48 := by
  obtain ⟨hR, hfr, hw, hnd, h, hE, hsz, henc⟩ := s3_issue_hyps
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := issue_pointer_soundC (ty := πA.ty) (ad := adA) hR hfr hw hnd h hE rfl hsz
    henc
  have hv : (a7.set tA).view 1 = tA := SC.view_set rfl
  have hm : mA10 = run mA9 (storeOps (Ty := Unit) πA.pe mA9 πA.L πA.ty tA a7.A.length 8) := by
    show run mA9 (realize πA wv (.issue 1 0 [5] 8) a7 arA mA9) = _
    rw [realize_issue πA wv hE]
    exact congrArg (fun t => run mA9 (storeOps (Ty := Unit) πA.pe mA9 πA.L πA.ty t a7.A.length 8))
      hv
  rw [hm]
  exact ⟨h1, h2, by decide⟩

end Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.ARRealize

232	`newMutex` is a library operation establishing a synchronized authority-administration entry. Let `slot` be the place holding `guarded`, `M` its immediate structural parent and `ctl = ControlOf(M,slot)` its controller leaf.
233	
234	**Preconditions**
235	
236	1. `guarded` is active, of own mode `Modify`, and legally held by the usable `slot`.
237	2. The constructing frame has ordinary exercisable `Modify` over `guarded` under Spec 1 §43.
238	3. The declared structural positions identify the usable `slot` and a usable controller **leaf** `ctl` in the same `M`.
239	4. `footprint(guarded) ∩ footprint(M) = ∅`. This is the reference mutex's structural disjointness requirement, allowing the control value `M` to be shared under compatible `Observe` authorities while `guarded` exclusively protects a distinct storage footprint.
240	5. If `guarded` is stored by O8, the construction respects O8.3. In the reference arrangement, the protected root `T` is owned by `M`, not by `slot`; its leaves are not thereby included in `footprint(M)`.

242	7. The `guarded` identity is not registered as a live administrative identity by any other registered administration. This is an unconditional candidate unified consistency guard, following the non-duplication principle of Spec 1 §56.
243	8. **Controller uniqueness:** no other live synchronization entry is associated with `ctl`. The association is injective among live entries.
244	9. No active descendant of `guarded` covers a leaf of `footprint(guarded)`.
245	10. **Initialization:** all structural leaves in `footprint(M)` are `Init` before construction. The operation does not implicitly initialize them. Storage merely owned by `M`, but structurally outside `footprint(M)`, is not included in this requirement solely by ownership.
246	
247	**Effect**
248	
249	The library registers an initially available `SyncEntry { guarded, grant = none }`, without creating another access authority over the protected storage or initializing any leaf of `M`. Library administration state remains separate from `S_C`.

260

263	```
264	
265	The registry is supplied by the library contract and is not part of the kernel state `S_C`. It must refer to the same logical registry state used for the candidate library transition.
266	
267	For the reference mutex, the library's **authorization facts**, and only these facts, are:
268

270	2. That entry has `grant = none`.
271	3. The requesting frame has the required effective and exercisable access to `ControlOf(entry)` under the controller-access obligation corresponding to Spec 1 §68.2.

## C13. Reference Construction — `newMutex`

`newMutex` is a library operation establishing a synchronized authority-administration entry. Let `slot` be the place holding `guarded`, `M` its immediate structural parent and `ctl = ControlOf(M,slot)` its controller leaf.

**Preconditions**

1. `guarded` is active, of own mode `Modify`, and legally held by the usable `slot`.
2. The constructing frame has ordinary exercisable `Modify` over `guarded` under Spec 1 §43.
3. The declared structural positions identify the usable `slot` and a usable controller **leaf** `ctl` in the same `M`.
4. `footprint(guarded) ∩ footprint(M) = ∅`. This is the reference mutex's structural disjointness requirement, allowing the control value `M` to be shared under compatible `Observe` authorities while `guarded` exclusively protects a distinct storage footprint.
5. If `guarded` is stored by O8, the construction respects O8.3. In the reference arrangement, the protected root `T` is owned by `M`, not by `slot`; its leaves are not thereby included in `footprint(M)`.
6. `K.SharedMutable(ctl)` holds for the controller leaf.
7. The `guarded` identity is not registered as a live administrative identity by any other registered administration. This is an unconditional candidate unified consistency guard, following the non-duplication principle of Spec 1 §56.
8. **Controller uniqueness:** no other live synchronization entry is associated with `ctl`. The association is injective among live entries.
9. No active descendant of `guarded` covers a leaf of `footprint(guarded)`.
10. **Initialization:** all structural leaves in `footprint(M)` are `Init` before construction. The operation does not implicitly initialize them. Storage merely owned by `M`, but structurally outside `footprint(M)`, is not included in this requirement solely by ownership.

**Effect**

The library registers an initially available `SyncEntry { guarded, grant = none }`, without creating another access authority over the protected storage or initializing any leaf of `M`. Library administration state remains separate from `S_C`.

**Preservation obligation:** The construction must establish the entire `SyncInv` and `GrantDiscipline` suite for the new and previously live entries. This is not an additional resulting-state precondition.

**Interface and realization obligations:** The safe public interface must prevent falsification of the positional controller association (C13.3); the controller synchronization protocol (C13.6) must be enforced; and the initial physical controller state must correspond to the newly available abstract registry entry. These are not claimed to follow from the authority-only state `S_C`.

A reference representation may place the protected value in a distinct logical owned-storage root. No separate physical allocation is implied.

## C14. Concurrent External Contract — `SyncAuthorized`

`K_C` extends the unchanged Spec 1 contract `K`. The proposed concurrent authorization predicate accepts the **current logical synchronization registry as an explicit external argument**:

```
K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, sync_registry, guarded, requesting_frame)
```

The registry is supplied by the library contract and is not part of the kernel state `S_C`. It must refer to the same logical registry state used for the candidate library transition.

For the reference mutex, the library's **authorization facts**, and only these facts, are:

1. There exists a live registered entry with the requested `guarded` identity.
2. That entry has `grant = none`.
3. The requesting frame has the required effective and exercisable access to `ControlOf(entry)` under the controller-access obligation corresponding to Spec 1 §68.2.

The library must prove, under `ConcurrentWF`, the applicable Spec 1 invariants, `SyncInv`, `GrantDiscipline`, and the abstraction's encapsulation contract, that these facts imply the remaining authority prerequisites for `deriveSync`, including origin-chain validity, sufficient effective mode, absence of blocking descendants and I1 conservation.

The opaque authorization predicate must not be defined by simply conjoining the conclusions the library is required to prove. Its instantiation is state-dependent, and correctness must be reestablished for every enabled acquisition.

`SyncAuthorized` does not create an authority, does not introduce ambient context rights, and cannot be used outside the corresponding valid synchronization contract. The precise synchronized physical realization remains deferred under `OB-C05`.

## C15. New Concurrent Transition — `deriveSync`

`deriveSync` is a new candidate concurrent transition creating an ordinary derived `Modify` authority from `guarded` over `footprint(guarded)`.

**Preconditions**

1. **Own-mode bound, retained from Spec 1 §43 and O1.1:** `guarded` is active and its **own mode permits `Modify`**. In the `Observe | Modify` mode order this requires own mode `Modify`, **even if `footprint(guarded)` is empty**.
2. The complete applicable origin-chain and effective-anchor validity requirements of O1.1 hold.
3. **Exclusive authorization:** `K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, sync_registry, guarded, current_frame)` holds. This predicate is the **only** authorization for `deriveSync`. Neither the current-frame-holder nor the place-holder alternative of ordinary `ExercisableAt` independently enables this new transition. Ordinary O1 retains both alternatives unchanged.
4. O1.2's leaf, subfootprint and effective-mode conditions hold for the full protected footprint and requested mode `Modify`.
5. O1.3's structural exclusivity and I1 preservation conditions hold.
6. O1.4's freshness, legal current-frame holder and resulting-state validity conditions hold.

**Effect**

A fresh, active authority is created with own mode `Modify`, origin `guarded`, full footprint `footprint(guarded)`, and holder equal to the executing context's current frame. No other access right is created.

This grant is ordinary after creation: `ExercisableAt` remains exactly as in Spec 1 §43 for its exercise, reborrowing, storage and legal release. The synchronized exception concerns **only the authorization for creating this derivative**; it does not weaken the source activity, own-mode bound, anchor, effective-mode or structural exclusivity requirements of O1.

**Outcome:** `ok` or `reject` for the abstract safety transition; a busy controller may make the enclosing library acquisition temporarily non-enabled, as specified in C16.

## C16. Reference Acquisition — `acquire`

The library operation `acquire` combines synchronization-controller acquisition and `deriveSync` into one coherent abstract operation.

The library must establish all non-dynamic safety preconditions before committing a successful acquisition.

Its success:

1. acquires the controller under the applicable synchronization protocol;
2. creates the valid grant through `deriveSync`;
3. records the resulting grant identity in `SyncEntry.grant`.

No partially successful abstract operation may expose an invalid ordinary state.

A temporarily held controller may leave acquisition non-enabled without producing `reject`.

The exact physical atomicity and event semantics are deferred.

## C17. Reference Unlock — `unlock`

s.set (deriveEff (s.view c) g ((s.view c).afp g) .modify)

/-- Preconditions of `deriveSync(guarded)` executed by `c` with the registry `r` (WC4 C15.1–C15.6):
those of O1 (Spec 1 §60) for `source = guarded`, `region = footprint(guarded)`, `mode = Modify`,
on the view of `c`, with `K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, r, guarded, current frame)` in place of
`ExercisableAt(source, Modify)` of §60.1 as the only authorization (WC4 C15.3). -/
structure DeriveSyncPre {R : Type} (kc : KC R) (r : R) (s : SC) (c g : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C15.1, Spec 1 §60.1: `source` is active. -/
  active : (s.view c).Active g
  /-- WC4 C15.1 (Spec 1 §43, §60.1): the own mode of `guarded` permits `Modify`. -/
  mode : OptP ((s.view c).A[g]?) (fun y => Mode.modify.le y.mode) False
  /-- WC4 C15.3: `deriveSync` is authorized exclusively through `K_C.SyncAuthorized`. -/
  authorized : kc.SyncAuthorized r s g (s.view c).top
  /-- WC4 C15.2, Spec 1 §60.1: every authority of the origin chain of `source` is active. -/
  chainActive : ∀ x ∈ (s.view c).ancs g, (s.view c).Active x
  /-- WC4 C15.4, Spec 1 §60.2: the leaves of `region` exist. -/
  leaves : ∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, l < s.P.length ∧ isLeaf s.P l
  /-- WC4 C15.4, Spec 1 §60.2: the leaves of `region` belong to the footprint of `source`. -/
  within : ∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, l ∈ (s.view c).afp g
  /-- WC4 C15.4, Spec 1 §60.2: `Modify` does not exceed the effective right of `source` on these
  leaves. -/
  modeOK : ∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, Allows (effective (s.view c) g l) .modify
  /-- WC4 C15.5, Spec 1 §60.3: the addition preserves I1 (§50). -/
  exclusive : ∀ b ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
    b ∉ g :: (s.view c).ancs g → (∃ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, l ∈ y.footprint) →
      y.mode = .observe ∧ Mode.modify = .observe) True
  /-- WC4 C15.6, Spec 1 §60.4: the new holding frame is the live current frame. -/
  frameLive : (s.view c).top ∈ (s.view c).F

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `deriveSync` (WC4 C15). -/
instance {R : Type} (kc : KC R) (r : R) (s : SC) (c g : Nat)
    [Decidable (kc.SyncAuthorized r s g (s.view c).top)] : Decidable (DeriveSyncPre kc r s c g) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((s.view c).Active g ∧
    OptP ((s.view c).A[g]?) (fun y => Mode.modify.le y.mode) False ∧
    kc.SyncAuthorized r s g (s.view c).top ∧
    (∀ x ∈ (s.view c).ancs g, (s.view c).Active x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, l < s.P.length ∧ isLeaf s.P l) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, l ∈ (s.view c).afp g) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, Allows (effective (s.view c) g l) .modify) ∧
    (∀ b ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
      b ∉ g :: (s.view c).ancs g → (∃ l ∈ (s.view c).afp g, l ∈ y.footprint) →
        y.mode = .observe ∧ Mode.modify = .observe) True) ∧
    (s.view c).top ∈ (s.view c).F)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i⟩⟩

/-- `deriveSync(guarded)` executed by `c` with the registry `r` (WC4 C15): `ok` or `reject`; no
outcome if `c` is not live. -/
def DeriveSyncStep {R : Type} (kc : KC R) (r : R) (s : SC) (c g : Nat) (o : Outcome3 SC) : Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ Guarded (DeriveSyncPre kc r s c g) (deriveSyncEff s c g) o

109-  { k with SyncAuthorized := LibSyncAuthorized L }
110-

112-instance (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) (g f : Nat) :
113-    Decidable ((libKC k L).SyncAuthorized reg s g f) :=
114-  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (LibSyncAuthorized L reg s g f))

120-  ∀ g f, kc.SyncAuthorized reg s g f → ∃ e ∈ reg, e.guarded = g ∧ e.Live s
121-
122-/-- The library instantiation satisfies the obligation of WC4 C14. -/

# Spec 2, jalon 3 — passe de clôture

Branche `formal/spec2-m3`. Exploratoire, jamais mergée ; rien n'est poussé, aucune PR.

- **Sources :** `ERN_WC4.md` (WC4 corrigée, celle du jalon 3) ; `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v3, verdicts de référence ; Spec 1 `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- **Fichiers non modifiés :** `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `formal/DESIGN.md`, `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/`.
- **Invariants inchangés :** rien n'est ajouté à `Encap`, `SyncInv`, `ArenaInvC` ni `AdminSep`.
- **Hors périmètre :** P1 et P3 restent des choix du modèle exploratoire. P7 reste ouvert.
- **Index consolidé :** `spec2-m3.md`, partie B, mis à jour en place.

Chemins relatifs à `formal/Ern/Concurrency/`. Numéros de ligne à `bf36d25`.

## Commits

| Commit | Tâche |
|---|---|
| `d007962` | 1 — S10 dans le noyau séquentiel |
| `faa2a0f` | 2 — exécution de S3 réalisée jusqu'à `issue` |
| `eb017a5` | 3 — `ArenaReg.unique` |
| `8903979` | 4 — témoins de passation |
| `bf36d25` | 5 — docstrings du corpus v3, suite concurrente de S10, `W_C22_2_cycle` |
| commit suivant | rapports : `spec2-m3.md` en place, ce fichier |

## Tâche 1 — S10 séquentiel (`Corpus/S10Seq.lean`)

Le module n'importe que `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main`. La configuration S10 est montée sans mutex : `M = {slot}` possède `T` ; `guarded` est rangée dans `slot` ; `g := derive(guarded, Modify)` est tenue par `f0`. Contrat `Examples.K0`. Mise en place : `s10seq_setup` (`:52`).

| Pas | Attendu | Obtenu | Clause | Théorème |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. `transfer(M, M′)` depuis `f1` | `ok` | `ok` | Spec 1 §63.1, §63.4, §63.7 | `S10Seq_1_ok` (`Corpus/S10Seq:62`) |
| 2. `exitFrame` | `reject` | `reject` | §73.4 | `S10Seq_2_reject` (`:66`) |
| 3. `EffAnchorOK … g (some f0)` | faux | faux | ni §44 ni §63.7 ne contraignent `g` | `S10Seq_anchor_misplaced` (`:74`) |
| 4. `transfer(M′, M)` | `ok` | `ok` | §63.3 | `S10Seq_3_ok` (`:78`) |
| 5. `exitFrame` | `ok` | `ok` | §73.4, §73.5 | `S10Seq_4_ok` (`:82`) |

Les états des pas 2 et 5 sont atteignables depuis `S3.init s10st` sous `K0` (`s10seq_reachable`, `:87`). Aucun verdict ne diffère.

## Tâche 2 — S3 réalisé jusqu'à `issue` (`Corpus/ARRealize.lean`)

- **`SimRunC` concrète.** `ar_sim0` … `ar_sim10` (`:55`–`114`) : de l'état initial du bloc AR au pas 3 de S3 (`acquire(e2)`, puis `issue(arena, R1, d1)`). Chaque pas porte son `StepOblC`, par `decide`. Paramètres : `πA := piOf a8.P []` ; `ParamsOK` par `piOf_ok`.
- **`s3_realized`** (`:123`). L'exécution est réalisée depuis la mémoire vide par des pas bruts `ok`, sans `ub`. `ReprC` tient aux 11 états. Les étiquettes forment une `EncapsulatedTrace` depuis l'état initial.
- **`s3_issue_hyps`** (`:152`). Les hypothèses d'`issue_pointer_soundC` tiennent ensemble avant `issue` : `ReprC`, `FramesC`, `WF3`, `NoDangling`, le pas `ok` `S3_3_ok`, l'entrée d'arène, la taille de la feuille et `PtrEncAt`.
- **`s3_issue_pointer`** (`:164`). Les octets de `d1` décodent l'adresse `adA`, avec la provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective ; `adA = 48`.
- **Verdicts et clauses.** Pas 2 et 3 attendus `ok`, obtenus `ok` et réalisés. Clauses : Spec 1 §77, §82.2, §82.3 ; WC4 C19, C25.

## Tâche 3 — `ArenaReg.unique`

- **(a) impossible.** `ArenaInvC` n'entraîne pas l'unicité : `arenaInvC_not_unique` (`Corpus/AR:201`) établit `ArenaInvC a6 (arA ++ arA) ∧ ¬ ArenaReg.unique (arA ++ arA) a6`.
- **(b) fait**, comme invariant de trace séparé :
  - `ArenaReg.unique` (`ArenaPreserve:488`), Spec 1 §56, première phrase ;
  - `lstep_arenaUnique` (`ArenaPreserve:522`) : tout `LStep` la préserve. Hypothèses : l'unicité avant, et la borne des `internal` enregistrés (fournie par `ArenaInvC` le long d'une trace) ;
  - `trace_arenaUnique`, `encapsulated_arenaUnique` (`Reachable:155`, `:168`) : forme trace, puis depuis l'état initial ;
  - `ar_unique` (`Corpus/AR:208`) : non-vacuité sur le registre de S3.
- **Énoncés non touchés.** L'unicité n'entre ni dans `LibInv`, ni dans les hypothèses de T4 (`lstep_preserves`) ou de T7 (`lstep_arenaInv`). Ces énoncés sont inchangés.

# Spec 2, jalon 3 — passe de clôture

Branche `formal/spec2-m3`. Exploratoire, jamais mergée ; rien n'est poussé, aucune PR.

- **Sources :** `ERN_WC4.md` (WC4 corrigée, celle du jalon 3) ; `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v3, verdicts de référence ; Spec 1 `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- **Fichiers non modifiés :** `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `formal/DESIGN.md`, `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/`.
- **Invariants inchangés :** rien n'est ajouté à `Encap`, `SyncInv`, `ArenaInvC` ni `AdminSep`.
- **Hors périmètre :** P1 et P3 restent des choix du modèle exploratoire. P7 reste ouvert.
- **Index consolidé :** `spec2-m3.md`, partie B, mis à jour en place.

Chemins relatifs à `formal/Ern/Concurrency/`. Numéros de ligne à `bf36d25`.

## Commits

| Commit | Tâche |
|---|---|
| `d007962` | 1 — S10 dans le noyau séquentiel |
| `faa2a0f` | 2 — exécution de S3 réalisée jusqu'à `issue` |
| `eb017a5` | 3 — `ArenaReg.unique` |
| `8903979` | 4 — témoins de passation |
| `bf36d25` | 5 — docstrings du corpus v3, suite concurrente de S10, `W_C22_2_cycle` |
| commit suivant | rapports : `spec2-m3.md` en place, ce fichier |

## Tâche 1 — S10 séquentiel (`Corpus/S10Seq.lean`)

Le module n'importe que `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main`. La configuration S10 est montée sans mutex : `M = {slot}` possède `T` ; `guarded` est rangée dans `slot` ; `g := derive(guarded, Modify)` est tenue par `f0`. Contrat `Examples.K0`. Mise en place : `s10seq_setup` (`:52`).

| Pas | Attendu | Obtenu | Clause | Théorème |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. `transfer(M, M′)` depuis `f1` | `ok` | `ok` | Spec 1 §63.1, §63.4, §63.7 | `S10Seq_1_ok` (`Corpus/S10Seq:62`) |
| 2. `exitFrame` | `reject` | `reject` | §73.4 | `S10Seq_2_reject` (`:66`) |
| 3. `EffAnchorOK … g (some f0)` | faux | faux | ni §44 ni §63.7 ne contraignent `g` | `S10Seq_anchor_misplaced` (`:74`) |
| 4. `transfer(M′, M)` | `ok` | `ok` | §63.3 | `S10Seq_3_ok` (`:78`) |
| 5. `exitFrame` | `ok` | `ok` | §73.4, §73.5 | `S10Seq_4_ok` (`:82`) |

Les états des pas 2 et 5 sont atteignables depuis `S3.init s10st` sous `K0` (`s10seq_reachable`, `:87`). Aucun verdict ne diffère.

## Tâche 2 — S3 réalisé jusqu'à `issue` (`Corpus/ARRealize.lean`)

- **`SimRunC` concrète.** `ar_sim0` … `ar_sim10` (`:55`–`114`) : de l'état initial du bloc AR au pas 3 de S3 (`acquire(e2)`, puis `issue(arena, R1, d1)`). Chaque pas porte son `StepOblC`, par `decide`. Paramètres : `πA := piOf a8.P []` ; `ParamsOK` par `piOf_ok`.
- **`s3_realized`** (`:123`). L'exécution est réalisée depuis la mémoire vide par des pas bruts `ok`, sans `ub`. `ReprC` tient aux 11 états. Les étiquettes forment une `EncapsulatedTrace` depuis l'état initial.
- **`s3_issue_hyps`** (`:152`). Les hypothèses d'`issue_pointer_soundC` tiennent ensemble avant `issue` : `ReprC`, `FramesC`, `WF3`, `NoDangling`, le pas `ok` `S3_3_ok`, l'entrée d'arène, la taille de la feuille et `PtrEncAt`.
- **`s3_issue_pointer`** (`:164`). Les octets de `d1` décodent l'adresse `adA`, avec la provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective ; `adA = 48`.
- **Verdicts et clauses.** Pas 2 et 3 attendus `ok`, obtenus `ok` et réalisés. Clauses : Spec 1 §77, §82.2, §82.3 ; WC4 C19, C25.

## Tâche 3 — `ArenaReg.unique`

- **(a) impossible.** `ArenaInvC` n'entraîne pas l'unicité : `arenaInvC_not_unique` (`Corpus/AR:201`) établit `ArenaInvC a6 (arA ++ arA) ∧ ¬ ArenaReg.unique (arA ++ arA) a6`.
- **(b) fait**, comme invariant de trace séparé :
  - `ArenaReg.unique` (`ArenaPreserve:488`), Spec 1 §56, première phrase ;
  - `lstep_arenaUnique` (`ArenaPreserve:522`) : tout `LStep` la préserve. Hypothèses : l'unicité avant, et la borne des `internal` enregistrés (fournie par `ArenaInvC` le long d'une trace) ;
  - `trace_arenaUnique`, `encapsulated_arenaUnique` (`Reachable:155`, `:168`) : forme trace, puis depuis l'état initial ;
  - `ar_unique` (`Corpus/AR:208`) : non-vacuité sur le registre de S3.
- **Énoncés non touchés.** L'unicité n'entre ni dans `LibInv`, ni dans les hypothèses de T4 (`lstep_preserves`) ou de T7 (`lstep_arenaInv`). Ces énoncés sont inchangés.

## Tâche 4 — témoins de passation (`Corpus/Handoff.lean`, corpus § 2 bis)

Chaque trace est une `EncapsulatedTrace` depuis un état initial `SC.ofS3 (S3.init …)`. `KInvC` tient à l'état final par `encapsulated_inv`. Les docstrings citent le corpus et n'affirment ni ordre ni absence de course.

| Témoin, pas | Attendu | Obtenu | Clause | Théorème (`Corpus/Handoff`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W-HO, mise en place | S13 | réutilise `S13_1_reject` | — | `w_ho_trace` (`:44`) |
| W-HO 1, 2, 3 | `ok`, `ok`, `ok` (`c1` vivant au pas 3) | idem | O10.1 ; O3.1–O3.3 ; O10.1, §40, §43.2 | `W_HO_1_ok` (`:29`), `W_HO_2_ok` (`:33`), `W_HO_3_ok` (`:39`) ; jumeau `S13_2_ok` (`Corpus/Frames:149`) cité |
| W-HO′, mise en place, `spawn` cédant `a`, `b` gardée par `f0` | `ok` | `ok` | WC4 C4.3, C4.5, O6.3 | `W_HO2_0_ok` (`Corpus/Handoff:76`) |
| W-HO′ 1 | `reject` | `reject` ; mode effectif de `a` absent | O10.1, §43.3 | `W_HO2_1_reject` (`:83`) |
| W-HO′ 2, 3, 4 | `ok`, `ok`, `ok` | idem | O10.1 ; O3 ; §43.2 | `W_HO2_2_ok` (`:87`), `W_HO2_3_ok` (`:91`), `W_HO2_4_ok` (`:95`), `w_ho2_trace` (`:100`) |
| W-HO″, mise en place | `ok` | `ok` ; parent de la frame initiale de `c2` : frame 1 | O1, C4 | `w_ho3_setup` (`:137`) |
| W-HO″ 1, 2, 3 | `ok`, `ok`, `ok` | idem | O10.1 ; O3 ; O3.3 | `W_HO3_1_ok` (`:144`), `W_HO3_2_ok` (`:148`), `W_HO3_3_ok` (`:153`) |
| W-HO″ 4, `terminate` avec `c2` vivant | `ok` ; reparentage sur `f0` | `ok` ; `c2` vivant ; **parent obtenu : frame 0** (frame 1 avant) | WC4 C7, C6 | `W_HO3_4_ok` (`:159`) |
| W-HO″ 5, 6 | `ok`, `ok` (`c2` vivant) | idem | C8 ; O10.1, §43.2 | `W_HO3_5_ok` (`:164`), `W_HO3_6_ok` (`:168`), `w_ho3_trace` (`:178`) |
| W-HO″, négatif : `release(a)` avant `release(a₂)` | `reject` | `reject` ; `a₂` active | O3.3 | `W_HO3_7_reject` (`:173`) |

Aucun verdict ne diffère. Le `spawn` de W-HO′ est `ok`.

## Tâche 5 — synchronisation documentaire

- **Docstrings alignées sur la v3** (`bf36d25`) :
  - S10 : module, `S10_1_ok` ;
  - S11 : `S11_setup_wait`, `S11_1_ok` ;
  - W-C22.2 : `W_C22_2_encap`, `W_C22_2_reenable` ;
  - S3 négatif : `S3_3b_reject`, §60.2 en premier ;
  - S16 (c) : `ctl_transfer_breaks_ctlInit`.
- **S12.** Aucune docstring ne disait « déjà encodé » ; rien à changer.
- **S16 (c) n'est pas renommé en `Z`.** Le témoin utilise la place `Y`, place 7 des statiques `est`, aussi destination de S16 (a). Un `Z` distinct demanderait une place de plus dans `est`, donc d'autres états pour tout `EncapTraces.lean` : docstring seule.
- **`spec2-m3.md`.** Table de § A.3 mise à jour (S3 négatif, S9, S10, S11, S12, S16, S17, S18, W-C22.2). Une ligne de clôture est ajoutée à P1–P4, P6–P9. Partie B : modules, théorèmes, corpus de clôture, obligations OB-C08, OB-C12 et OB-C16, audit, et « Ce qui n'est pas vérifié ». Les numéros de ligne ont été relevés à `bf36d25` par un script qui ne fait que signaler, puis corrigés à la main.

## Écarts

1. **Ajouts au-delà des docstrings (tâche 5).** Ils encodent des verdicts de la v3 absents du module concurrent :
   - `S10_2_ok` (`Corpus/S10:73`) et `S10_3_ok` (`:79`) : suite concurrente de S10, `transfer(M′, M)` `ok` admis par `Encap`, puis `exitFrameC(f1)` `ok` ;
   - `W_C22_2_cycle` (`Corpus/MX:379`) : fondement renforcé de C22.2. Le cycle `acquire`/`unlock` du contexte 1 depuis `MX₄` atteint `(x5r, regX)`, l'état et le registre atteints par le `deriveSync` brut suivi du `release`.
2. **Base de la branche.** Après `fe2f4ee` viennent les trois commits de la revue : `8e2bccf`, `33b672f`, `e645f62`. La passe part de `e645f62`.
3. **P7 : deux verdicts du corpus et son critère § 0.** Le critère dit qu'une clause d'autorité ou de la Spec 1 défaillante donne `reject`. Or le corpus donne `non habilité` dans deux cas où la clause défaillante est de ce type :
   - **Mise en place de S11 sans la cession d'`o1′`** (`S11_setup_wait`, `Corpus/MX:259`). Le corpus : « sans elle C14.3/§68.2 échoue et `acquire` n'est pas habilité ». C14.3 renvoie à §68.2, une clause d'accès.
   - **W-C22.2** (`W_C22_2_encap`, `Corpus/MX:349`). Le corpus : `acquire(e)` « non habilitée tant que la dérivée sauvage est active (C13.9/C14) ». Dans `x5`, pour les contextes 0 et 1, `SyncAuthorized` est vrai (faits C14.1–C14.3). Ce qui échoue est `modeOK` (C15.4, Spec 1 §60.2) et `exclusive` (C15.5, §60.3), évalués par `#eval` sur `DeriveSyncPre`.
   - Le modèle ne distingue pas les deux verdicts pour `acquire`, qui ne définit que `ok`. Les encodages restent tels quels, comme le demande le brief ; l'arbitrage appartient au critère P7.

## Audit final des axiomes

- **Méthode.** `collectAxioms` sur toutes les constantes `thmInfo` `Ern.Concurrency*` et `_private.Ern.Concurrency*`, après `import Ern`.
- **Résultat à `bf36d25`.** 1144 théorèmes, dont 886 non internes, contre 1092 (835) au jalon 3. Aucun axiome hors `{propext, Quot.sound}`, y compris pour les théorèmes des tâches 1 à 5.
- **Build.** `lake build` réussit (69 jobs), sans avertissement.
- **Recherches vides.** Le `grep` d'`AGENTS.md` est vide. Aucun `noncomputable`, `decide +kernel` ni `ofReduceBool` dans `formal/Ern/Concurrency/`.
- **Fichiers intouchés.** `git diff e645f62 --stat` ne touche ni `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/` ni les fichiers protégés.
- **Lignes longues.** Aucune ligne ajoutée ne dépasse 100 caractères.
