tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

remaining_plan.description: What is left to do: steps, files, what done looks like.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Corpus adversarial — ERN Spec 2, jalon 3 (v6)

**v6** — après la mise à jour du rapport `spec2-m4-handoff.md` (test de `ChainExcl`) : statut de W-GC mis à jour ; ajout du témoin W-GS (§ 2 sexies). Aucun verdict de la v5 n'est modifié. **v5** — après le rapport `spec2-m4-handoff.md` : W-GR est confirmé par le modèle ; ajout du témoin W-GC (§ 2 quinquies) ; précision sur la mise en place de S10b. Aucun verdict de la v4 n'est modifié. **v4** — après le rapport de clôture `spec2-m3-close.md` : deux verdicts alignés sur le critère P7 (mise en place de S11, W-C22.2), ajout du témoin W-GR (§ 2 ter) et du cas S10b (§ 2 quater). Aucun autre verdict n'est modifié. **v3** — ajout des témoins de passation (§ 2 bis) ; aucun verdict de la v2 n'est modifié. **v2** — corrections après le rapport `spec2-m3.md` et sa revue ; chaque changement est listé en § 5. Les verdicts corrigés le sont depuis la Spec 1 et WC4, pas depuis le modèle.

Document de travail, non normatif, joint au brief du jalon 3. Dérivé des règles de la Spec 1 v0.1 et de WC4 corrigée ; aucun verdict ne vient du modèle Lean. Chaque rejet a un jumeau positif. Les cas sont des traces de pas abstraits, sans syntaxe.

## 0. Conventions

- `c0` : contexte initial, frame de base `f0` ; `fk` : frames entrées par `enterFrame` ; `c1`, `c2` : contextes créés par `spawn`.
- `root_X` : autorité racine `Modify` de la place `X`, détenue par son owner (§40, `RootHeld`).
- **Verdicts** : `ok` ; `reject` ; `fail` (seulement `alloc` et `issue`, §58, §77.4) ; `non habilité` (aucune issue : attente, WC4 C8, C16) ; `ok noyau / hors C22` (pas `ok` de la machine, refusé par `Encap`, WC4 C22–C23) ; `hors fragment` (dépend d'OB-C01 à OB-C06).
- **`reject` / `non habilité`** (critère P7, à arbitrer) : une clause de **synchronisation** défaillante (contrôleur occupé C16, `grant ≠ none` C14.2) rend l'opération `non habilitée` ; une clause d'**autorité ou de registre** défaillante (C17.2, C18.1, toute clause de la Spec 1) donne `reject`. La durée ne joue pas : un `reject` peut cesser (S11.3 après `join`), un `non habilité` peut durer (S11.2). WC4 C17/C18 ne définissent que `ok` : leur `reject` est encodé par l'absence d'issue `ok` plus la clause défaillante.
- Les réalisations mémoire (jalon 2) ne sont pas répétées. Chaque pas `ok` d'un cas est **éligible** à une réalisation sous les paramètres (`ParamsOK`) et les obligations par pas (`StepOblC`) du jalon 2 ; l'acceptation abstraite n'établit pas ces obligations.

### Bloc MX — mutex de référence (WC4 C12–C13)

Dans `f0` : `M = {slot, lock}`, `lock` `Init` et `K.SharedMutable lock`, `slot` `Uninit` ; `T` racine possédée par `M`, feuilles `Init`.
1. `guarded := derive(root_T, Modify, footprint(T))` — O1, `root_T` détenue par `M`, `f0` a `Modify` sur `M`.
2. `store(guarded, slot)` — O8 ; `slot` devient `Init` ; O8.3 satisfaite (`T` possédée par `M`, pas par `slot`).
3. `newMutex(guarded)` → entrée `e`, `ControlOf(e) = lock` — C13.1–10 (C13.10 : `slot`, `lock` `Init`).
4. Partage : `o1 := derive(root_M, Observe, {slot, lock})` ; `spawn c1` cédant `o1`. Après quoi `root_M` a mode effectif `Observe` sur `{slot, lock}` (§43.4) : `CtrlRight` tient pour `f0` et pour la frame initiale de `c1`.

**Deux états nommés.** `MX₃` = étapes 1–3, mutex **non partagé** : `f0` a `Modify` effectif sur `M`, donc O4.1 (`transfer` de source dans `M`) et §69.1 (`endUse` d'une place de `M`) sont satisfaites au noyau ; c'est l'état des cas qui isolent une clause de C22. `MX₄` = étapes 1–4, mutex **partagé** : `f0` n'a plus que `Observe` effectif sur `M` ; `transfer`, `endUse`, `resetLock` depuis `f0` sont rejetés au noyau ou par C18.1, ce qui est voulu dans S7 négatif et S11.

### Bloc AR — arena synchronisée (WC4 C19 ; Spec 1 §§46, 76–78)

Dans `f0` : `M2 = {slot2, lock2}` comme MX ; `AV` feuille racine possédée par `M2`, `Init` ; `ST` racine possédée par `f0`, structurée en régions `R1`, `R2` disjointes.
1. `internal := derive(root_ST, Modify, footprint(ST))` ; `store(internal, AV)` ; `newArena(ST, internal)` — O17 ; la valeur d'arena est `AV` (§46, §76.3).
2. `guarded2 := derive(root_AV, Modify, {AV})` ; `store(guarded2, slot2)` ; `newMutex(guarded2)` → `e2`, `ControlOf(e2) = lock2` ; C13.4 : `{AV} ∩ {slot2, lock2} = ∅` ; C19 : le grant couvrira toute la valeur d'arena.
3. Partage de `M2` à `c1` comme en MX.

## 1. Cas
## 2 quinquies. Témoin W-GC — exercice à travers `guarded` (ajout v5)

**Origine.** Ce cas a été découvert par la formalisation (contre-exemple `Corpus/GuardedChain.lean`, rapport `spec2-m4-handoff.md`). Les verdicts ci-dessous sont re-dérivés ici de la Spec 1 ; ils ne sont pas repris du modèle.

**Mise en place.** Bloc MX, plus un local `Y` de `f0`, une feuille, `Init`. Avant `newMutex` : `z := derive(root_Y, Modify)` ; `store(z, T)` (O8 : `T` feuille utilisable sous `Modify` de `f0`, `z` ne couvre pas `T`). Puis les étapes 1 à 4 du bloc MX : `guarded`, `store(guarded, slot)`, `newMutex(guarded)`, partage par `o1` cédée à `c1`.

| Pas | Verdict attendu au noyau, fondement |
|---|---|
| 1. `c1 : read3(Y)` avec `access = z` | `ok` — O9.2 : `ExercisableAt(z, Observe)` par la troisième clause de §43 appliquée **deux fois** : `z` est tenue par `T` ; sur les feuilles de `T`, `guarded` est exerçable en `Observe` avec un mode effectif `Modify` ; `guarded` est tenue par `slot`, sur les feuilles duquel `o1` est exerçable en `Observe`. `effective(z, Y) = Modify` |
| 2. `c0 : acquire(e)` | `ok` — C14.1–3, C15 |
| 3. `c0 : write3(Y)` avec `access = z` | `ok` — O10.1 : `ExercisableAt(z, Modify)` ; `z` est tenue par `T`, sur les feuilles duquel le grant `g`, tenu par `f0`, est exerçable en `Modify` |
| 4. `c0 : read3(Y)` avec `access = z`, sous le grant | `ok` — comme le pas 3, en `Observe` |

**Encapsulation.** Sous `Encap`, et sous une exclusion qui ne regarde que l'autorité passée en argument, les pas 1 à 3 sont admis : l'argument est `z`, pas `guarded`. Sous la règle « aucun droit utilisé par un pas n'est justifié à travers un `guarded` vivant » : le pas 1 est **exclu**, sa justification passe par `guarded` ; les pas 2, 3 et 4 sont **admis**, la justification des pas 3 et 4 passe par le grant. **Obtenu par le modèle** pour les opérations à argument d'autorité exercé (`ChainExcl`, `Encap5C` ; `gc_read_excluded`, `lc_trace`, rapport `spec2-m4-handoff.md`, § Test de la correction).

**Ce que le témoin montre.** Fermer l'accès direct à `guarded` ne suffit pas : tout ce que la donnée protégée tient est atteignable de la même façon. L'exclusion doit porter sur la chaîne de détention entière, et elle doit laisser intact l'accès par le grant.

## 2 sexies. Témoin W-GS — écriture dans la donnée protégée sans verrou, par un droit sur une place (ajout v6)

**Verdicts attendus, tirés de la Spec 1 et de WC4, pas encore vérifiés par le modèle.** Le témoin vise les opérations dont le droit est un droit sur une place (`HasRight`), que `ChainExcl` ne couvre pas dans son état actuel.

**Mise en place.** `MX₃` (mutex non partagé, `grant = none`), plus un local `Y2` de `f0`, une feuille, `Init`. Puis :

- `z2 := derive(root_Y2, Modify)` ;
- partage **partiel** : `o := derive(root_M, Observe, {lock})` — l'empreinte ne couvre que le contrôleur. `root_M` garde un mode effectif `Modify` sur `slot` et passe à `Observe` sur `lock` (§43.4) ;
- `spawn c1` cédant `o`.

| Pas | Verdict attendu au noyau, fondement |
|---|---|
| 1. `c0 : store(z2, T)`, sans grant | `ok` — O8.2 : `T` est sous `Modify` exerçable de `f0`, par `guarded` : `guarded` est tenue par `slot`, sur les feuilles duquel `root_M` est exerçable en `Modify` avec un mode effectif `Modify` (troisième clause de §43), et `effective(guarded, T) = Modify`. O8.1, O8.3, O8.4, O8.5 satisfaites (`z2` tenue par `f0`, ne couvre pas `T` ; ancre de `z2` et place `T` dans `f0`) |
| 2. `c1 : acquire(e)` | `ok` — C14.1, C14.2 ; C14.3 : `o` donne à `c1` le droit d'accès au contrôleur ; C15 |
| 3. `c1 : read3(T)` via son grant | `ok` — O9 |
| Jumeau : `c0 : acquire(e)`, puis `c0 : store(z2, T)` sous son grant | `ok`, `ok` — le droit sur `T` repose sur le grant |

**Encapsulation.** Attendu : les pas 1 à 3 forment une trace admise par `Encap5C` — `store` n'a pas d'argument d'autorité exercé, et `ChainExcl` ne regarde pas son droit sur `T`. Sous la règle étendue aux droits sur les places : le pas 1 est **exclu** (seul `guarded` a un mode effectif `Modify` sur `T`) ; le jumeau est **admis**.

**Ce que le témoin montre, hors de ce corpus** (modèle d'événements, WC5 C27) : la réalisation de `store` écrit la feuille `T`. Le pas 1 est donc une écriture de la donnée protégée hors verrou, par le propriétaire, face à une lecture sous verrou d'un autre contexte créé avant elle. Le partage partiel est ce qui rend les deux possibles ensemble : le propriétaire garde `Modify` sur `slot` pendant qu'un autre contexte peut prendre le verrou.

## 3. Théorèmes de corpus

| Nom | Énoncé | Fondement |
|---|---|---|
| `CrossContextConflictOnlyShared` | Pour `c ≠ c′` vivants : si `WriteSharedPre (view c) a L` et `Read3Pre`, `Write3Pre` ou `WriteSharedPre (view c′) b L′`, alors toute feuille de `L ∩ L′` est `K.SharedMutable` | O11.1 (immédiat) ; complète R4 : le seul conflit inter-contextes habilité par la machine passe par `writeShared` sur une feuille `SharedMutable` |
| Témoin de `CrossContextConflictOnlyShared` | `MX₄` : `c0 : writeShared(lock)` via `root_M` et `c1 : read3(lock)` via `o1` **tous deux habilités** dans le même état ; `L ∩ L′ = {lock}` | O11.2, O9 ; c'est la surface exacte d'OB-C03/OB-C05 |
| Réduction (plan de preuve à consigner dans l'index, pas un théorème) | Une fois la data race définie en C/D (OB-C01, OB-C02), son absence devra se déduire de : R4, `CrossContextConflictOnlyShared`, la discipline des feuilles `SharedMutable` (OB-C03, OB-C05), et la réalisation des ordres d'autorité par `happens-before` (OB-C04, OB-C11). Ce n'est pas une équivalence formelle : la définition et les ordres appartiennent à C/D | Rapport du jalon 2, frontière de R4 |

## 4. Règles d'encodage

- Un théorème par verdict, nommé `S<cas>_<n>_<ok|reject|fail|wait|encap>` ; les jumeaux dans le même module.
- Préconditions décidées par `decide` ; verdict écrit **depuis ce document**, jamais ajusté au modèle. Un désaccord entre le verdict attendu et le modèle est un **résultat** : rapporter la clause et l'état, ne corriger ni l'un ni l'autre en silence.
- `non habilité` : `∀ st′, ¬ Op … st′`. `ok noyau / hors C22` : `opStepC … (.ok _) ∧ ¬ Encap …`, avec la clause d'invariant qui tombe sans l'exclusion.
- `hors fragment` : aucun théorème ; mention dans le rapport.

**Ce que le témoin montre, hors de ce corpus** (modèle d'événements, WC5 C27) : la réalisation de `store` écrit la feuille `T`. Le pas 1 est donc une écriture de la donnée protégée hors verrou, par le propriétaire, face à une lecture sous verrou d'un autre contexte créé avant elle. Le partage partiel est ce qui rend les deux possibles ensemble : le propriétaire garde `Modify` sur `slot` pendant qu'un autre contexte peut prendre le verrou.

| Nom | Énoncé | Fondement |
|---|---|---|
| `CrossContextConflictOnlyShared` | Pour `c ≠ c′` vivants : si `WriteSharedPre (view c) a L` et `Read3Pre`, `Write3Pre` ou `WriteSharedPre (view c′) b L′`, alors toute feuille de `L ∩ L′` est `K.SharedMutable` | O11.1 (immédiat) ; complète R4 : le seul conflit inter-contextes habilité par la machine passe par `writeShared` sur une feuille `SharedMutable` |

Ce n'est pas une équivalence formelle : la définition et les ordres appartiennent à C/D | Rapport du jalon 2, frontière de R4 |

## 4. Règles d'encodage

- Un théorème par verdict, nommé `S<cas>_<n>_<ok|reject|fail|wait|encap>` ; les jumeaux dans le même module.
- Préconditions décidées par `decide` ; verdict écrit **depuis ce document**, jamais ajusté au modèle. Un désaccord entre le verdict attendu et le modèle est un **résultat** : rapporter la clause et l'état, ne corriger ni l'un ni l'autre en silence.

import Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.MX

# Counterexample: exercise through `guarded` in a holder chain

Brief of milestone 4, task 4. `GuardedExcl` excludes the steps whose authority argument is a live
`guarded`, while the third clause of Spec 1 §43 is recursive along the holder chain: an authority
`z` stored in the protected `T` is exercisable by any frame that can exercise `guarded`, held by
`slot`, in `Observe`. The trace below is built from the initial state of Spec 1 §47 with the
contract `KM` of `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v4 §0; each step is an `ok` step admitted by `Encap5`, by
`decide`. It refutes `cap5_sound` and `handoff_loss_exists`.

Statics: `0` the mutex value `M` with fields `1` (`slot`, `Uninit`) and `2` (`lock`, `Init`), `3`
the protected root `T` (`Init`) owned by `M`, `4` a local `Y` (`Init`) of the base frame. Root
authorities: `0` of `M` (frame 0), `1` of `T` (held by `M`), `2` of `Y` (frame 0).
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.GuardedChain

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.Concurrency Ern.Concurrency.Corpus
open Ern.Concurrency.Traces (L0)

/-- Statics (Spec 1 §47): block MX of `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v4 §0 without `M′`, and a local `Y`. -/
def zst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), true),
   ((none, some 0, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), true)]

/-- The statics are well formed (Spec 1 §47). -/
theorem zst_ok : StaticsOK zst := by decide

/-- Initial state (Spec 1 §47). -/
def gc0 : SC := SC.ofS3 (S3.init zst)
/-- `z := derive(root_Y, Modify)`, authority 3 (O1). -/
def gc1 : SC := gc0.set (deriveEff (gc0.view 0) 2 [4] .modify)
/-- `store(z, T)` (O8): `z` is held by `T`. -/
def gc2 : SC := storeEffC gc1 0 3 3
/-- `guarded := derive(root_T, Modify, footprint(T))`, authority 4 (O1). -/
def gc3 : SC := gc2.set (deriveEff (gc2.view 0) 1 [3] .modify)
/-- `store(guarded, slot)` (O8). -/
def gc4 : SC := storeEffC gc3 0 4 1
/-- The registry after `newMutex(guarded)` (WC4 C13). -/
def greg : SyncReg := [⟨4, none⟩]
/-- `o1 := derive(root_M, Observe, {slot, lock})`, authority 5 (O1). -/
def gc5 : SC := gc4.set (deriveEff (gc4.view 0) 0 [1, 2] .observe)
/-- `spawn c1` yielding `o1` (WC4 C4): context 1, initial frame 1. -/
def gc6 : SC := spawnEff gc5 0 [5] []
/-- `c1 : read3(Y)` via `z` (O9): the state is unchanged. -/
def gc7 : SC := gc6.set (gc6.view 1)
/-- `c0 : acquire(e)`: grant `g`, authority 6, held by frame 0 (WC4 C16). -/
def gc8 : SC := deriveSyncEff gc7 0 4
/-- The registry with the grant recorded (WC4 C16). -/
def gregG : SyncReg := [⟨4, some 6⟩]
/-- `c0 : write3(Y)` via `z` (O10). -/
def gc9 : SC := gc8.set (write3Eff (gc8.view 0) [4])

/-- The labels of the trace. -/
def glbls : List Label :=
  [.kernel 0 (.derive 2 [4] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 3), .kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify),
   .kernel 0 (.store 4 1), .newMutex 0 4, .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [1, 2] .observe), .spawn 0 [5] [],
   .kernel 1 (.read 3 [4]), .acquire 0 0, .kernel 0 (.write 3 [4])]

/-- The setup up to `MX₄` with `z` stored in `T`: each step is an `ok` step admitted by `Encap5`
(Spec 1 §60, §65; WC4 C4, C13). -/
theorem gc_setup : EncapsulatedTrace5 KM L0 (gc0, [], []) (glbls.take 7) (gc6, greg, []) :=
  .cons ⟨(fun e he => by cases he), (fun e he => by cases he), trivial⟩
    (.kernel ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.kernel ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨(fun e he => by cases he), (fun e he => by cases he), trivial⟩
    (.kernel ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.kernel ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.newMutex ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨(by decide : ∀ e ∈ greg, e.Live gc4 → 0 ≠ e.guarded),
      (by decide : ∀ e ∈ greg, e.Live gc4 → 0 ≠ e.guarded), trivial⟩
    (.kernel ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.spawn ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩) .nil

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.
## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization

A leaf's initialization state and the effective right to access it are two distinct conditions.

## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
## C14. Concurrent External Contract — `SyncAuthorized`

`K_C` extends the unchanged Spec 1 contract `K`. The proposed concurrent authorization predicate accepts the **current logical synchronization registry as an explicit external argument**:

```
K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, sync_registry, guarded, requesting_frame)
```

The registry is supplied by the library contract and is not part of the kernel state `S_C`. It must refer to the same logical registry state used for the candidate library transition.

For the reference mutex, the library's **authorization facts**, and only these facts, are:

1. There exists a live registered entry with the requested `guarded` identity.
2. That entry has `grant = none`.
3. The requesting frame has the required effective and exercisable access to `ControlOf(entry)` under the controller-access obligation corresponding to Spec 1 §68.2.

The library must prove, under `ConcurrentWF`, the applicable Spec 1 invariants, `SyncInv`, `GrantDiscipline`, and the abstraction's encapsulation contract, that these facts imply the remaining authority prerequisites for `deriveSync`, including origin-chain validity, sufficient effective mode, absence of blocking descendants and I1 conservation.

The opaque authorization predicate must not be defined by simply conjoining the conclusions the library is required to prove. Its instantiation is state-dependent, and correctness must be reestablished for every enabled acquisition.

`SyncAuthorized` does not create an authority, does not introduce ambient context rights, and cannot be used outside the corresponding valid synchronization contract. The precise synchronized physical realization remains deferred under `OB-C05`.

## C15. New Concurrent Transition — `deriveSync`

import Ern.Concurrency.CapDrop

/-!
# Test of a corrected `GuardedExcl`

`GuardedExcl` (brief of milestone 4, task 3) excludes the steps whose authority argument is a live
`guarded`; the third clause of Spec 1 §43 is recursive along the holder chain, and an authority
stored in the protected storage is exercisable through `guarded` (`Corpus/GuardedChain.lean`).
This module tests the correction proposed in `formal/reports/spec2-m4-handoff.md`: the authority
argument of `derive`, `split`, `read`, `write` and `writeShared` must be exercisable from the
current frame by a holder chain that contains no live `guarded` (`Exer5`). It is a proposition of
the report, absent from WC5 and from the brief, tested here and not decided. Beside it, the
definitions of the brief (`GuardedExcl`, `Encap5`, `EncapsulatedTrace5`) are unchanged.
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Exercise without a live `guarded` -/

/-- `ExercisableAt` (Spec 1 §43) read from the current frame of `c`, by a holder chain none of whose
authorities is the `guarded` of a live entry of `reg` (WC4 C12). -/
inductive Exer5 (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) : Nat → Mode → Prop where
  | base {a : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : NotGuarded s reg a → s.A[a]? = some y →
      y.active = true → m.le y.mode → y.holder = .frame (s.view c).top → Exer5 s reg c a m
  | held {a p b : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : NotGuarded s reg a → s.A[a]? = some y →
      y.active = true → m.le y.mode → y.holder = .place p → Exer5 s reg c b m →
      (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s.flat b l) m) → Exer5 s reg c a m

/-- One step of `Exer5 · m` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure, on the pattern of `exR`,
Spec 1 §43). -/
def exer5R (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) (m : Mode) (E : Nat → Bool) (a : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (NotGuarded s reg a) && match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => y.active && decide (m.le y.mode) && match y.holder with
    | .frame f => decide (f = (s.view c).top)
    | .place p => (List.range s.A.length).any fun b =>
        decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s.flat b l) m) && E b
  | none => false

/-- `exer5R` is a bounded monotone rule. -/
theorem exer5R_rule (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) (m : Mode) :
    KRule s.A.length (exer5R s reg c m) where
  mono p q hpq a h := by
    unfold exer5R at h ⊢
    simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
    refine ⟨h.1, ?_⟩
    have h2 := h.2
    split at h2
    · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h2 ⊢
      refine ⟨h2.1, ?_⟩; split at h2
      · simpa using h2.2
      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, List.any_eq_true] at h2 ⊢
        obtain ⟨b, hb, hc, he⟩ := h2.2
        exact ⟨b, hb, hc, hpq b he⟩
    · exact h2
  bound p a h := by
    unfold exer5R at h
    simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
    have h2 := h.2
    (hm : m.le y.mode) (hp : y.holder = .place p) (hb : b < s.A.length)
    (hc : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s.flat b l) m) (hE : E b = true) :
    exer5R s reg c m E a = true := by
  simp only [exer5R, hy, ha, hp, Bool.true_and, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
    List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
  exact ⟨hg, hm, b, hb, hc, hE⟩

/-- `Exer5` is computed by `|A| + 1` steps of `exer5R`. -/
theorem exer5_iff {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {c a : Nat} {m : Mode} :
    Exer5 s reg c a m ↔ kiter (exer5R s reg c m) (s.A.length + 1) a = true := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, exer5_of_kiter s reg c m _ a⟩
  induction h with
  | base hg hy ha hm hf => exact exer5R_base hg hy ha hm hf
  | held hg hy ha hm hp _ hc ih =>
    rw [← kiter_fix (exer5R_rule s reg c _)]
    exact exer5R_held hg hy ha hm hp (kiter_bound (exer5R_rule s reg c _) _ _ ih) hc ih

/-- Decidability of `Exer5`. -/
instance (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (Exer5 s reg c a m) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ exer5_iff.symm

/-- An authority exercisable without a live `guarded` from the current frame of a context with a
nonempty stack is attributable to that context without a live `guarded` (WC5 C43). -/
theorem Exer5.attr5 {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {c a : Nat} {m : Mode} (hne : s.stk c ≠ [])
    (h : Exer5 s reg c a m) : Attr5 s reg c a m := by
  induction h with
  | base hg hy ha hm hf => exact .base hg hy ha hm hf (view_top_mem hne)
  | held hg hy ha hm hp _ hc ih => exact .held hg hy ha hm hp ih hc

/-- The argument of an `Exer5` is not a live `guarded`. -/
theorem Exer5.notGuarded {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {c a : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : Exer5 s reg c a m) :
    NotGuarded s reg a := by
  cases h with
  | base hg => exact hg
  | held hg => exact hg

/-! ## The corrected exclusion -/

/-- `ChainExcl` (correction proposed in `formal/reports/spec2-m4-handoff.md`, tested here): the
authority argument of `derive` (Spec 1 §60.1), `split` (§61.1), `read` (§66.2), `write` (§67.1) and
`writeShared` (§68.2) is exercisable, in the mode the precondition requires, from the current
frame of the executing context by a holder chain without a live `guarded` (`Exer5`). -/
def ChainExcl (st : SC × SyncReg) : Label → Prop
  | .kernel c (.derive a _ m) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a m
  | .kernel c (.split a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .modify
  | .kernel c (.read a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .observe
  | .kernel c (.write a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .modify
  | .kernel c (.writeShared a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .observe
  | _ => True

/-- Decidability of `ChainExcl`. -/
instance (st : SC × SyncReg) (lbl : Label) : Decidable (ChainExcl st lbl) := by
  unfold ChainExcl; split <;> infer_instance

/-- `Encap5C`: `Encap5` with `ChainExcl` in place of `GuardedExcl`. -/
def Encap5C (L : MutexLayout) (st : SC × SyncReg) (lbl : Label) : Prop :=
  Encap L st lbl ∧ ChainExcl st lbl ∧ CtlExcl L st lbl

/-- `ChainExcl` implies `GuardedExcl`: the argument of an `Exer5` is not a live `guarded`. -/
theorem chainExcl_guardedExcl {st : SC × SyncReg} {lbl : Label} (h : ChainExcl st lbl) :
    GuardedExcl st lbl := by
  cases lbl with
  | kernel c op =>
    cases op <;> simp only [ChainExcl, GuardedExcl] at h ⊢ <;>
      first | trivial | exact h.notGuarded
  | _ => trivial

/-- `EncapsulatedTrace5C`: a run every step of which satisfies `Encap5C` in the state where it is
taken. -/
inductive EncapsulatedTrace5C (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) :
    SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → List Label → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → Prop where
  | nil {st : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st [] st
  | cons {st st₁ st₂ : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {lbl : Label} {lbls : List Label} :
      Encap5C L (st.1, st.2.1) lbl → LStep k L lbl st st₁ →
      EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st₁ lbls st₂ → EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st (lbl :: lbls) st₂

/-- Every `EncapsulatedTrace5C` is an `EncapsulatedTrace5`: `cap5_compat` and `cap5_drop_own`
apply to it. -/
theorem encapsulatedTrace5C_imp {k : K} {L : MutexLayout} {st st' : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg}
    {lbls : List Label} (h : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st lbls st') :
    EncapsulatedTrace5 k L st lbls st' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact .nil
  | cons he hs _ ih => exact .cons ⟨he.1, chainExcl_guardedExcl he.2.1, he.2.2⟩ hs ih

/-- An `EncapsulatedTrace5C` extended by one step satisfying `Encap5C`. -/
theorem EncapsulatedTrace5C.snoc {k : K} {L : MutexLayout}
    {st st' st'' : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {lbls : List Label} {lbl : Label}
    (h : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st lbls st') (he : Encap5C L (st'.1, st'.2.1) lbl)
    (hs : LStep k L lbl st' st'') : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st (lbls ++ [lbl]) st'' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact .cons he hs .nil
  | cons he' hs' _ ih => exact .cons he' hs' (ih he hs)

import Ern.Concurrency.CapDrop

/-!
# Test of a corrected `GuardedExcl`

`GuardedExcl` (brief of milestone 4, task 3) excludes the steps whose authority argument is a live
`guarded`; the third clause of Spec 1 §43 is recursive along the holder chain, and an authority
stored in the protected storage is exercisable through `guarded` (`Corpus/GuardedChain.lean`).
This module tests the correction proposed in `formal/reports/spec2-m4-handoff.md`: the authority
argument of `derive`, `split`, `read`, `write` and `writeShared` must be exercisable from the
current frame by a holder chain that contains no live `guarded` (`Exer5`). It is a proposition of
the report, absent from WC5 and from the brief, tested here and not decided. Beside it, the
definitions of the brief (`GuardedExcl`, `Encap5`, `EncapsulatedTrace5`) are unchanged.
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Exercise without a live `guarded` -/

/-- `ExercisableAt` (Spec 1 §43) read from the current frame of `c`, by a holder chain none of whose
authorities is the `guarded` of a live entry of `reg` (WC4 C12). -/
inductive Exer5 (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) : Nat → Mode → Prop where
  | base {a : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : NotGuarded s reg a → s.A[a]? = some y →
      y.active = true → m.le y.mode → y.holder = .frame (s.view c).top → Exer5 s reg c a m
  | held {a p b : Nat} {m : Mode} {y : Authority} : NotGuarded s reg a → s.A[a]? = some y →
      y.active = true → m.le y.mode → y.holder = .place p → Exer5 s reg c b m →
      (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s.flat b l) m) → Exer5 s reg c a m

/-- One step of `Exer5 · m` read on a Boolean premise (decision procedure, on the pattern of `exR`,
Spec 1 §43). -/
def exer5R (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) (m : Mode) (E : Nat → Bool) (a : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (NotGuarded s reg a) && match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => y.active && decide (m.le y.mode) && match y.holder with
    | .frame f => decide (f = (s.view c).top)
    | .place p => (List.range s.A.length).any fun b =>
        decide (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s.flat b l) m) && E b
  | none => false

/-- `exer5R` is a bounded monotone rule. -/
theorem exer5R_rule (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c : Nat) (m : Mode) :
    KRule s.A.length (exer5R s reg c m) where
  mono p q hpq a h := by
    unfold exer5R at h ⊢
    simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h ⊢
    refine ⟨h.1, ?_⟩
    have h2 := h.2
    split at h2
    · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h2 ⊢
      refine ⟨h2.1, ?_⟩; split at h2
      · simpa using h2.2
      · simp only [Bool.and_eq_true, List.any_eq_true] at h2 ⊢
        obtain ⟨b, hb, hc, he⟩ := h2.2
        exact ⟨b, hb, hc, hpq b he⟩
    · exact h2
  bound p a h := by
    unfold exer5R at h
    simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at h
    have h2 := h.2
    (hm : m.le y.mode) (hp : y.holder = .place p) (hb : b < s.A.length)
    (hc : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s.flat b l) m) (hE : E b = true) :
    exer5R s reg c m E a = true := by
  simp only [exer5R, hy, ha, hp, Bool.true_and, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
    List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
  exact ⟨hg, hm, b, hb, hc, hE⟩

/-- `Exer5` is computed by `|A| + 1` steps of `exer5R`. -/
theorem exer5_iff {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {c a : Nat} {m : Mode} :
    Exer5 s reg c a m ↔ kiter (exer5R s reg c m) (s.A.length + 1) a = true := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, exer5_of_kiter s reg c m _ a⟩
  induction h with
  | base hg hy ha hm hf => exact exer5R_base hg hy ha hm hf
  | held hg hy ha hm hp _ hc ih =>
    rw [← kiter_fix (exer5R_rule s reg c _)]
    exact exer5R_held hg hy ha hm hp (kiter_bound (exer5R_rule s reg c _) _ _ ih) hc ih

/-- Decidability of `Exer5`. -/
instance (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (Exer5 s reg c a m) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ exer5_iff.symm

/-- An authority exercisable without a live `guarded` from the current frame of a context with a
nonempty stack is attributable to that context without a live `guarded` (WC5 C43). -/
theorem Exer5.attr5 {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {c a : Nat} {m : Mode} (hne : s.stk c ≠ [])
    (h : Exer5 s reg c a m) : Attr5 s reg c a m := by
  induction h with
  | base hg hy ha hm hf => exact .base hg hy ha hm hf (view_top_mem hne)
  | held hg hy ha hm hp _ hc ih => exact .held hg hy ha hm hp ih hc

/-- The argument of an `Exer5` is not a live `guarded`. -/
theorem Exer5.notGuarded {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {c a : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : Exer5 s reg c a m) :
    NotGuarded s reg a := by
  cases h with
  | base hg => exact hg
  | held hg => exact hg

/-! ## The corrected exclusion -/

/-- `ChainExcl` (correction proposed in `formal/reports/spec2-m4-handoff.md`, tested here): the
authority argument of `derive` (Spec 1 §60.1), `split` (§61.1), `read` (§66.2), `write` (§67.1) and
`writeShared` (§68.2) is exercisable, in the mode the precondition requires, from the current
frame of the executing context by a holder chain without a live `guarded` (`Exer5`). -/
def ChainExcl (st : SC × SyncReg) : Label → Prop
  | .kernel c (.derive a _ m) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a m
  | .kernel c (.split a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .modify
  | .kernel c (.read a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .observe
  | .kernel c (.write a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .modify
  | .kernel c (.writeShared a _) => Exer5 st.1 st.2 c a .observe
  | _ => True

/-- Decidability of `ChainExcl`. -/
instance (st : SC × SyncReg) (lbl : Label) : Decidable (ChainExcl st lbl) := by
  unfold ChainExcl; split <;> infer_instance

def Encap5C (L : MutexLayout) (st : SC × SyncReg) (lbl : Label) : Prop :=

theorem chainExcl_guardedExcl {st : SC × SyncReg} {lbl : Label} (h : ChainExcl st lbl) :
    GuardedExcl st lbl := by
  cases lbl with
  | kernel c op =>
    cases op <;> simp only [ChainExcl, GuardedExcl] at h ⊢ <;>
      first | trivial | exact h.notGuarded
  | _ => trivial

taken. -/
inductive EncapsulatedTrace5C (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) :
    SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → List Label → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg → Prop where
  | nil {st : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st [] st
  | cons {st st₁ st₂ : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {lbl : Label} {lbls : List Label} :
      Encap5C L (st.1, st.2.1) lbl → LStep k L lbl st st₁ →
      EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st₁ lbls st₂ → EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st (lbl :: lbls) st₂

apply to it. -/

    {lbls : List Label} (h : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st lbls st') :
    EncapsulatedTrace5 k L st lbls st' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact .nil
  | cons he hs _ ih => exact .cons ⟨he.1, chainExcl_guardedExcl he.2.1, he.2.2⟩ hs ih

    {st st' st'' : SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg} {lbls : List Label} {lbl : Label}
    (h : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st lbls st') (he : Encap5C L (st'.1, st'.2.1) lbl)
    (hs : LStep k L lbl st' st'') : EncapsulatedTrace5C k L st (lbls ++ [lbl]) st'' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact .cons he hs .nil
  | cons he' hs' _ ih => exact .cons he' hs' (ih he hs)

def Run5C (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (σ : Nat → SC × SyncReg × ArenaReg) (lbls : List Label) :

    obtain ⟨ls, hls⟩ := run5C_prefix h n (by omega)
    obtain ⟨he, hs⟩ := h n (by omega)
    exact ⟨ls ++ [lbls[n]], hls.snoc he hs⟩

/-- `cap5_sound` with `Encap5C` and `EncapsulatedTrace5C` in place of `Encap5` and

import Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.GuardedChain

/-!
# Corpus v6, witness W-GS

`corpus-spec2-m3.md` v6 §2 sexies, W-GS: a write into the protected data without the lock, by a
right over a place. From `MX₃` (`grant = none`) with a local `Y2` of the base frame, the setup
derives `z2 := derive(root_Y2, Modify)`, shares only the controller by
`o := derive(root_M, Observe, {lock})` and spawns `c1` yielding `o`. One theorem per verdict,
written from `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v6 §2 sexies, preconditions by `decide`, contract `KM`.

Statics: those of `Corpus/GuardedChain.lean` (`zst`), place `4` being `Y2`. Root authorities: `0` of
`M` (frame 0), `1` of `T` (held by `M`), `2` of `Y2` (frame 0).
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.GuardedStore

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.Concurrency Ern.Concurrency.Corpus
open Ern.Concurrency.Corpus.GuardedChain (zst)
open Ern.Concurrency.Traces (L0)

/-- Initial state (Spec 1 §47). -/
def gs0 : SC := SC.ofS3 (S3.init zst)
/-- `guarded := derive(root_T, Modify, footprint(T))`, authority 3 (O1). -/
def gs1 : SC := gs0.set (deriveEff (gs0.view 0) 1 [3] .modify)
/-- `store(guarded, slot)` (O8). -/
def gs2 : SC := storeEffC gs1 0 3 1
/-- The registry after `newMutex(guarded)` (WC4 C13): `MX₃`. -/
def sreg : SyncReg := [⟨3, none⟩]
/-- `z2 := derive(root_Y2, Modify)`, authority 4 (O1). -/
def gs3 : SC := gs2.set (deriveEff (gs2.view 0) 2 [4] .modify)
/-- `o := derive(root_M, Observe, {lock})`, authority 5 (O1). -/
def gs4 : SC := gs3.set (deriveEff (gs3.view 0) 0 [2] .observe)
/-- `spawn c1` yielding `o` (WC4 C4): context 1, initial frame 1. -/
def gs5 : SC := spawnEff gs4 0 [5] []
/-- Step 1, `c0 : store(z2, T)` (O8): `z2` is held by `T`. -/
def gs6 : SC := storeEffC gs5 0 4 3
/-- Step 2, `c1 : acquire(e)`: grant `g₁`, authority 6, held by frame 1 (WC4 C16). -/
def gs7 : SC := deriveSyncEff gs6 1 3
/-- The registry with the grant recorded (WC4 C16). -/
def sregG : SyncReg := [⟨3, some 6⟩]
/-- Step 3, `c1 : read3(T)` via `g₁` (O9): the state is unchanged. -/
def gs8 : SC := gs7.set (gs7.view 1)
/-- Twin, `c0 : acquire(e)`: grant `g₀`, authority 6, held by frame 0 (WC4 C16). -/
def gt6 : SC := deriveSyncEff gs5 0 3
/-- Twin, `c0 : store(z2, T)` under `g₀` (O8). -/
def gt7 : SC := storeEffC gt6 0 4 3

/-- The labels of the setup. -/
def setupLbls : List Label :=
  [.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .modify), .kernel 0 (.store 3 1), .newMutex 0 3,
   .kernel 0 (.derive 2 [4] .modify), .kernel 0 (.derive 0 [2] .observe), .spawn 0 [5] []]

/-- The setup of `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v6 §2 sexies from the initial state: each step is an `ok`
step admitted by `Encap5C` (Spec 1 §60, §65; WC4 C4, C13). -/

  .cons ⟨(fun e he => by cases he), by decide, trivial⟩
    (.kernel ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.kernel ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.newMutex ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨(by decide : ∀ e ∈ sreg, e.Live gs2 → 2 ≠ e.guarded), by decide, trivial⟩
    (.kernel ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨(by decide : ∀ e ∈ sreg, e.Live gs3 → 0 ≠ e.guarded), by decide, trivial⟩
    (.kernel ⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩) <|
  .cons ⟨trivial, trivial, trivial⟩ (.spawn ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩) .nil

/-- `corpus-spec2-m3.md` v6 §2 sexies W-GS, step 1, `ok` (O8; O8.2 through `guarded` held by
`slot`, on whose leaves `root_M` is exercisable in `Modify` with effective mode `Modify`, Spec 1
§43, third clause): `store(z2, T)` by context 0 without the grant. -/

context 1, whose `o` gives the controller access; `g₁` is held by frame 1. -/

/-- Authority `g` grounds the right `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43; §63.4, §69.2, §70.3: "the
exercisable authority on which that right rests"): it is exercisable at `m` and its effective mode
permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
def Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=
  g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m

/-- Decidability of `Grounds` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Decidable (Grounds s m q g) := by
  unfold Grounds; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` is the grounding authority `g` or belongs to its origin chain (§63.4, §69.2,
§70.3: "the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain"). -/
def RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g

/-- Decidability of `RightChain` (§63.4, §69.2, §70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Decidable (RightChain s g j) := by
  unfold RightChain; infer_instance

/-- The clauses of O4 (Spec 1 §63) for the by-value argument `(src, dst)`, executed by the creating
context `c`, at the start of its transfer phase in state `t` (WC4 C5.2, C5 items 1, 3, 4): those
of `TransferPreC` other than the exercisable `Modify` over the destination (replaced by C5 item 2,
WC4 C5 item 3) and the resulting-state clauses; §63.8 is evaluated on the final state `fin` (WC4
C5.4). -/
structure ValTransferPre (k : K) (fin : S3) (t : SC) (c src dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C5 item 1, Spec 1 §63.1: `source` is usable. -/
  srcUsable : (t.view c).Usable src
  /-- Spec 1 §63.1: `destination` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : (t.view c).Usable dst
  /-- WC4 C5.2, C5 item 1, Spec 1 §63.1: exercisable `Modify` of the creating frame over the
  source. -/
  srcRight : HasRight (t.view c) .modify src
  /-- WC4 C5.2, Spec 1 §63.2: same shape of ordered subtrees. -/
  sameShape : SameShape (t.view c).P src dst
  /-- WC4 C5 item 1, Spec 1 §63.3: all source leaves are `Init`. -/
  srcInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint (t.view c).P src, (t.view c).I l = .init
  /-- WC4 C5 item 2, Spec 1 §63.3: no destination leaf is `Init`. -/
  dstNotInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint (t.view c).P dst, (t.view c).I l ≠ .init
  /-- WC4 C5.2, Spec 1 §63.3: disjoint footprints. -/
  disjoint : ¬ overlap (t.view c).P src dst
  /-- WC4 C5.2, C5 item 4, Spec 1 §63.4: no active derived authority covers a source leaf from
  outside the source, except some authority grounding the `Modify` right over the source and its
  origin chain. -/
  noOutsideDerived : ∃ g ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length, Grounds (t.view c) .modify src g ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside (t.view c) src j →
      RightChain (t.view c) g j
  /-- WC4 C5 item 4, Spec 1 §63.5: no in-place source leaf is pinned. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ footprint (t.view c).P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ (t.view c).pin l = false
  /-- WC4 C5 item 4, Spec 1 §63.6, first half: dependencies of the usable places following the
  value are valid. -/
  depsValid : ∀ x ∈ movedDeps (t.view c) src, (t.view c).Active x
  /-- WC4 C5 item 4, C5.4, Spec 1 §63.8: no authority held before the transfer by a part of the
  source covers, in the final state, a leaf of its holder. -/
  noSelfLock : ∀ j ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length,
    OptP ((t.view c).A[j]?) (fun y => heldIn (t.view c).P src y.holder) False → ¬ SelfLock fin j

/-- Decidability of `ValTransferPre` (WC4 C5). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (fin : S3) (t : SC) (c src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (ValTransferPre k fin t c src dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((t.view c).Usable src ∧ (t.view c).Usable dst ∧
    HasRight (t.view c) .modify src ∧ SameShape (t.view c).P src dst ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (t.view c).P src, (t.view c).I l = .init) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (t.view c).P dst, (t.view c).I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap (t.view c).P src dst ∧
    (∃ g ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length, Grounds (t.view c) .modify src g ∧
      ∀ j ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside (t.view c) src j →
        RightChain (t.view c) g j) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (t.view c).P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ (t.view c).pin l = false) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ movedDeps (t.view c) src, (t.view c).Active x) ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length,
      OptP ((t.view c).A[j]?) (fun y => heldIn (t.view c).P src y.holder) False →
        ¬ SelfLock fin j))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩⟩

/-- WC4 C5.2: every by-value argument satisfies `ValTransferPre` at the start of its transfer
phase, in the declared order, on the state produced by the earlier transfers. -/
def ValTransfersPre (k : K) (fin : S3) (c : Nat) : SC → List (Nat × Nat) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | t, v :: vs => ValTransferPre k fin t c v.1 v.2 ∧
      ValTransfersPre k fin c (transferEffC t c v.1 v.2) vs

/-- Decidability of `ValTransfersPre` (WC4 C5.2). -/
instance instDecidableValTransfersPre (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (fin : S3) (c : Nat) :
    (t : SC) → (vs : List (Nat × Nat)) → Decidable (ValTransfersPre k fin c t vs)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l⟩⟩

/-- The by-value composite executed by `c` (WC4 C5): `ok` or `reject`; no outcome if `c` is not
live. -/
def SpawnValStep (k : K) (s : SC) (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
    (vs : List (Nat × Nat)) (o : Outcome3 SC) : Prop :=
  s.Live c ∧ Guarded (SpawnValPre k s c ps ls vs) (spawnValEff s c ps ls vs) o
