tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

content.content:
## C12. Synchronization Registry

A reference library abstraction maintains logical entries:

```
SyncEntry {
    guarded: AuthorityId
    grant: Option<AuthorityId>
}
```

An entry is live exactly while `guarded` is active. This registry belongs to library abstraction state, not `S_C`.

A live entry requires an active `guarded` authority of own mode `Modify`, held by a usable place `slot` belonging structurally to a mutex value `M`, and a usable controller leaf `ctl` at its declared field position within `M`.

`ControlOf` is the **per-instance positional relationship**: it identifies `M` as the structural parent of `slot` at `guardedField`, then identifies `ctl` as the child of `M` at `controlField`. `M` and `slot` are structural places; storage owned by `M` is not automatically in `footprint(M)` under Spec 1 §40.

For distinct live mutex entries, both their `guarded` identities and their `ControlOf` controller leaves must be distinct.

A legal transfer of the **whole mutex value `M`**, or a structural ancestor containing `M`, may carry `slot` and its controller together and preserve the association positionally (`slot → slot′`, `ctl → ctl′`). This includes cases in which a grant is active, provided all O4 conditions hold. By contrast, the safe abstraction excludes independent transfers whose source is `slot`, a strict structural subplace of `slot`, or `ctl`, as specified in C22.3. Such restrictions do not redefine O4. A transfer of `M` as a whole, or of an enclosing root, remains eligible under O4's own preconditions; preservation of `SyncInv` is a separate proof obligation.

## C13. Reference Construction — `newMutex`

`newMutex` is a library operation establishing a synchronized authority-administration entry. Let `slot` be the place holding `guarded`, `M` its immediate structural parent and `ctl = ControlOf(M,slot)` its controller leaf.

**Preconditions**

1. `guarded` is active, of own mode `Modify`, and legally held by the usable `slot`.
2. The constructing frame has ordinary exercisable `Modify` over `guarded` under Spec 1 §43.
3. The declared structural positions identify the usable `slot` and a usable controller **leaf** `ctl` in the same `M`.
4. `footprint(guarded) ∩ footprint(M) = ∅`. This is the reference mutex's structural disjointness requirement, allowing the control value `M` to be shared under compatible `Observe` authorities while `guarded` exclusively protects a distinct storage footprint.
5. If `guarded` is stored by O8, the construction respects O8.3. In the reference arrangement, the protected root `T` is owned by `M`, not by `slot`; its leaves are not thereby included in `footprint(M)`.
6. `K.SharedMutable(ctl)` holds for the controller leaf.
7. The `guarded` identity is not registered as a live administrative identity by any other registered administration. This is an unconditional candidate unified consistency guard, following the non-duplication principle of Spec 1 §56.
8. **Controller uniqueness:** no other live synchronization entry is associated with `ctl`. The association is injective among live entries.
9. No active descendant of `guarded` covers a leaf of `footprint(guarded)`.
10. **Initialization:** all structural leaves in `footprint(M)` are `Init` before construction. The operation does not implicitly initialize them. Storage merely owned by `M`, but structurally outside `footprint(M)`, is not included in this requirement solely by ownership.

**Effect**

The library registers an initially available `SyncEntry { guarded, grant = none }`, without creating another access authority over the protected storage or initializing any leaf of `M`. Library administration state remains separate from `S_C`.

**Preservation obligation:** The construction must establish the entire `SyncInv` and `GrantDiscipline` suite for the new and previously live entries. This is not an additional resulting-state precondition.

**Interface and realization obligations:** The safe public interface must prevent falsification of the positional controller association (C13.3); the controller synchronization protocol (C13.6) must be enforced; and the initial physical controller state must correspond to the newly available abstract registry entry. These are not claimed to follow from the authority-only state `S_C`.

A reference representation may place the protected value in a distinct logical owned-storage root. No separate physical allocation is implied.

## C14. Concurrent External Contract — `SyncAuthorized`

`K_C` extends the unchanged Spec 1 contract `K`. The proposed concurrent authorization predicate accepts the **current logical synchronization registry as an explicit external argument**:

```
K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, sync_registry, guarded, requesting_frame)
```

The registry is supplied by the library contract and is not part of the kernel state `S_C`. It must refer to the same logical registry state used for the candidate library transition.

For the reference mutex, the library's **authorization facts**, and only these facts, are:

1. There exists a live registered entry with the requested `guarded` identity.
2. That entry has `grant = none`.
3. The requesting frame has the required effective and exercisable access to `ControlOf(entry)` under the controller-access obligation corresponding to Spec 1 §68.2.

The library must prove, under `ConcurrentWF`, the applicable Spec 1 invariants, `SyncInv`, `GrantDiscipline`, and the abstraction's encapsulation contract, that these facts imply the remaining authority prerequisites for `deriveSync`, including origin-chain validity, sufficient effective mode, absence of blocking descendants and I1 conservation.

The opaque authorization predicate must not be defined by simply conjoining the conclusions the library is required to prove. Its instantiation is state-dependent, and correctness must be reestablished for every enabled acquisition.

`SyncAuthorized` does not create an authority, does not introduce ambient context rights, and cannot be used outside the corresponding valid synchronization contract. The precise synchronized physical realization remains deferred under `OB-C05`.

## C15. New Concurrent Transition — `deriveSync`

`deriveSync` is a new candidate concurrent transition creating an ordinary derived `Modify` authority from `guarded` over `footprint(guarded)`.

**Preconditions**

1. **Own-mode bound, retained from Spec 1 §43 and O1.1:** `guarded` is active and its **own mode permits `Modify`**. In the `Observe | Modify` mode order this requires own mode `Modify`, **even if `footprint(guarded)` is empty**.
2. The complete applicable origin-chain and effective-anchor validity requirements of O1.1 hold.
3. **Exclusive authorization:** `K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, sync_registry, guarded, current_frame)` holds. This predicate is the **only** authorization for `deriveSync`. Neither the current-frame-holder nor the place-holder alternative of ordinary `ExercisableAt` independently enables this new transition. Ordinary O1 retains both alternatives unchanged.
4. O1.2's leaf, subfootprint and effective-mode conditions hold for the full protected footprint and requested mode `Modify`.
5. O1.3's structural exclusivity and I1 preservation conditions hold.
6. O1.4's freshness, legal current-frame holder and resulting-state validity conditions hold.

**Effect**

A fresh, active authority is created with own mode `Modify`, origin `guarded`, full footprint `footprint(guarded)`, and holder equal to the executing context's current frame. No other access right is created.

This grant is ordinary after creation: `ExercisableAt` remains exactly as in Spec 1 §43 for its exercise, reborrowing, storage and legal release. The synchronized exception concerns **only the authorization for creating this derivative**; it does not weaken the source activity, own-mode bound, anchor, effective-mode or structural exclusivity requirements of O1.

**Outcome:** `ok` or `reject` for the abstract safety transition; a busy controller may make the enclosing library acquisition temporarily non-enabled, as specified in C16.

## C16. Reference Acquisition — `acquire` **[WC5 MODIFIED — D-C1]**

The library operation `acquire` combines synchronization-controller acquisition and `deriveSync` into one coherent abstract operation.

**Outcome classification (proposed D-C1)**

1. **`reject` — invalid request:** a failure of entry existence/liveness (C14.1), controller-access authority (C14.3, including the applicable Spec 1 §68.2 contract), or any other applicable authority, register-validity, origin, footprint, invariant, or Spec 1 safety precondition yields `reject`. These failures remain `reject` even when the controller is occupied or `grant ≠ none` in the same state.
2. **Temporarily non-enabled — contention:** only after all non-contention validity and authority conditions hold, the entry's `grant ≠ none` (C14.2), or occupation of the controller by another acquisition under its valid protocol, makes `acquire` temporarily non-enabled. This is **not** `reject`, `fail`, or an additional `Outcome3` value; no successful transition is produced. Non-enablement may persist indefinitely.
3. **`ok` — successful acquisition:** all validity and authority obligations hold, the grant is available and the controller is successfully acquired under its protocol, and the successful effect below is established.

`reject` takes precedence over temporary non-enablement **for the same abstract state**; this is a classification of causes and does not assert that a concurrent call has an outcome independent of changing state. Resource `fail` outcomes of `alloc`/`issue` are outside this criterion.

For `acquire`, the authorization facts C14.1 and C14.3 are safety conditions; C14.2 is a contention condition. The combined `SyncAuthorized` predicate of C14 is therefore insufficient by itself to distinguish `reject` from temporary non-enablement. This does not alter the independent transition `deriveSync` or its C15 conditions.

The library must establish all non-dynamic safety preconditions before committing a successful acquisition.

Its success:

1. acquires the controller under the applicable synchronization protocol;
2. creates the valid grant through `deriveSync`;
3. records the resulting grant identity in `SyncEntry.grant`.

No partially successful abstract operation may expose an invalid ordinary state.

The controller's physical linearization, atomic ordering, and correspondence obligations are specified as proposals in C41, C48 and C49 and remain subject to `OB-C05`.

## C17. Reference Unlock — `unlock` **[WC5 MODIFIED — D-C1]**

`unlock` is a candidate derived library operation.

**Abstract preconditions**

1. A live entry has `grant = some g`.
2. `g` is active and legally releasable under O3.
3. No active descendant or surviving validity anchor prevents its release.
4. The acting frame has the applicable controller-access right, with effective mode present on `ControlOf(entry)` (Spec 1 §68.2).

**Proposed outcomes (D-C1)**

- **`ok`** if all applicable preconditions hold and the coherent effect below is completed.
- **`reject`** if any required entry, register, authority, dependency, O3-release, or controller-access condition fails, including a recorded `g` that has become inactive. Contention does not convert such a failure into temporary non-enablement.

This candidate defines no waiting outcome for `unlock` on a failed C17 precondition. A physical implementation may impose its own internal progress protocol, but it may not report an invalid request as a successful abstract unlock.

**Abstract effect**

The grant is released according to O3, the registry records `grant = none`, and the controller's logical synchronized state is made available as one coherent library transition.

**Realization obligation, not an assumed abstract precondition:** The controller update must satisfy `K.SharedMutable` and the required event, atomicity and ordering discipline. The physical protocol and its correspondence are specified provisionally in C41, C48 and C49 and remain under `OB-C05`, rather than being treated as proven by the abstract transition.

## C18. Abandoned Grants and Recovery **[WC5 MODIFIED — D-C1]**

A grant may become inactive through an inherited legal release or frame exit without a corresponding `unlock`; the live registry entry may still record `grant = some g`. This can leave the mutex unavailable indefinitely without itself violating memory safety.

`resetLock` is a candidate library recovery operation.

**Abstract preconditions**

1. Ordinary `ExercisableAt(guarded, Modify)` holds under Spec 1 §43, requiring the appropriate exclusive exercise through the mutex's holder.
2. No active descendant of `guarded` covers any protected leaf, as in the relevant no-descendant condition of Spec 1 §78.2.

# VIII. Conflicts, Ordering, and Consistency — Proposed Block C

## C30. Byte-Level Conflicts and Access Pairs

Two `acc` events from different execution contexts **conflict** if their concrete byte ranges intersect and at least one is a write. An RMW counts as both a read and a write for this purpose. Byte-level intersection is the criterion, even when each event corresponds to a larger logical leaf.

An `Atomic(size, align)` event is indivisible over the **entire concrete range of its leaf**; the fact that conflict detection is byte-based does not split that event into independently visible byte writes. Two read-only events do not conflict. Conflict is distinct from whether authority preconditions are satisfied, whether the events may overlap in wall-clock time, and whether a sufficient event-order relation exists. This distinction is essential for W-HO, W-HO′ and W-HO″.

## C31. Reads-From and Modification Order

The candidate graph contains:

- `rf` (**reads-from**): a relation from the write event whose value supplies a read component to the corresponding read event. Initial writes or initialized storage must have an explicitly represented source in any concrete litmus or proof requiring a read value.
- `mo` (**modification order**): for each `Atomic` location, a strict total order over **all writes/modifications of that location**, not merely atomic writes. This includes the represented initial/initializing write (including `newMutex` controller initialization) and any exclusive ordinary non-atomic write admitted under C42, as well as subsequent atomic stores and successful RMW modifications. Locations are the indivisible units fixed by C38, not arbitrary overlapping regions. Non-atomic initialization and exclusive writes remain **non-atomic** events; their inclusion in `mo` does not confer atomicity or `sw` on them.

For a successful atomic RMW, its read component obtains the immediately preceding modification of its atomic location in `mo`, under the chosen coherence model; a failed comparison observes a value via a read-only event and contributes no modification to `mo`. The first successful `acquire` must therefore be able to read (`rf`) the initializing `newMutex` write, which is explicitly included in `mo`. An ordinary exclusive write under C42 also occupies its appropriate `mo` position and must be `hb`-ordered as required by the applicable safe-access contract.

A well-formed graph must satisfy explicit typing, source-existence, range-identity, and coherence obligations on `rf` and `mo`. **Specifying `rf` and `mo` alone is insufficient to define a full permitted execution.** The fragment requires a named `EventConsistent` predicate (or equivalent) whose established conjuncts are listed in the corresponding proof statement. No unspecified or inconsistent graph may be accepted merely by postulating a convenient `rf` edge.

## C32. Synchronizes-With — `sw`

The following are **candidate reference** sources of synchronization:

1. **Atomic protocol:** a release-capable write/RMW (including a `seq_cst` store or RMW) and an acquire-capable read/RMW (including a `seq_cst` load or RMW) on the same atomic unit may establish `sw` when the acquire reads the release through the applicable `rf` relationship and the relevant memory orders provide release/acquire semantics. **Address identity alone is insufficient.** The initial Lean fragment uses **direct `rf`** only; release-sequence-mediated synchronization awaits explicit modeling.
2. **Context creation:** the parent's `spawn(c)` event `sw`-precedes the child's `start(c)` event, with all prior parent events and subsequent child events related through `po`.

A bare `spawn` in the abstract interleaving does not order parent operations executed **after** that `spawn` before the child's later operations. A `join(c)` orders only the events of the context whose completion it actually observes, subject to already established transitive edges; it does not implicitly join live descendants or unrelated contexts.

2. a synchronization event that establishes acquisition is `po`-before the corresponding logical **gain** marker (for example, an acquiring RMW preceding exposure of a mutex grant);
3. ordinary accesses protected by the gained authority occur `po`-after that gain marker.

These are **proposed semantic order obligations**. They must be validated against the compositional transition definitions and their possible realizations; they are not assumed consequences of the sequential kernel.

The obligation is that **each** physical access has the correct kind of authority, atomicity, footprint, and synchronization justification, not that all accesses are ordinary writes.

## C38. Atomic Units, Concrete Layouts, and Multi-Leaf Writes — D-C5

One `Atomic(size, align)` unit is **one logical leaf** whose entire byte range is a single physically supported atomic unit. The byte range may contain multiple bytes; an atomic 64-bit leaf occupying eight bytes is one event, not eight separately observable writes. The size must be supported for atomic operations on the target, and alignment and representation must satisfy `LayoutWF` and the applicable Spec 1 §82 obligations. Atomic event indivisibility and byte-range conflict testing are different properties.

An inherited `writeShared` whose region contains **more than one `Atomic` leaf** is **`reject`** under the proposed reading of O11.3: a multi-leaf region does not satisfy the indivisible-one-leaf `Atomic` discipline. It is not silently lowered into a sequence of independent atomics and is not a multiword transaction.

A region that combines incompatible `SharedDiscipline` classes is not automatically one legal `writeShared` step. It requires a separately established composite contract; in the initial WC5 reference discipline, such a region is `reject` as not satisfying a single applicable discipline. Multi-leaf regions classified consistently `Synchronized` or `Confined` remain eligible under O11 and their respective contracts, subject to all existing O11 preconditions.

No atomicity guarantee follows from word alignment alone or from merely declaring `K.SharedMutable`. A target that cannot realize the requested indivisible unit must reject the unsupported atomic contract or decline to expose it in a safe interface; it may not silently substitute a racy multi-step emulation.

## C39. Atomic Shared Writes and RMWs

The concurrent evaluation of inherited `writeShared` on an `Atomic` leaf carries a proposed memory-order annotation and produces **one indivisible atomic modification event**: a write, or an RMW when the declared atomic operation conditionally reads and modifies the same initialized leaf. The annotation and event kind refine the **concurrency contract and realization** of `writeShared`; they do not change the frozen O11 signature in `S₃`, its rights, its validity conditions, or its effect on initialization. If the atomic discipline, region, order, or realization requirements fail, the operation retains the existing O11 `reject` outcome.

**The kernel mutation underlying a successful atomic RMW is `writeShared` (O11), not a new mutation primitive.** A successful compare-and-exchange (CAS) on an initialized `Atomic` leaf is a `writeShared` mutation realized as one indivisible RMW event whose read component determines the conditional success and whose write component participates in `mo` (C31). **A failed CAS is a `readShared` (C37) observation**, represented by a non-modifying atomic read event: it neither invokes a successful O11 mutation nor creates an acquisition grant. A failed physical CAS attempt must still be recorded as a read in the realization's event graph. The comparison, chosen observed value, success/failure branch, and legal success/failure orders are constrained by `EventConsistent`, not by adding a state-local `rf` precondition to O11 or C37.

No general public CAS/RMW interface is specified by the frozen Spec 1. Specs 3/4 may expose a safe conditional atomic operation **implemented through the `writeShared`-on-success / `readShared`-on-failure contract above**; this does not permit any other kernel mutation under `Observe`. The reference mutex uses this contract internally under `OB-C05`.

## C40. Memory Orders and Operation Legality — D-C7

The proposed order set is:

```
{ relaxed, release, acquire, acq_rel, seq_cst }
```

`consume` is not included. **Proposed per-operation legality:**

  is rejected (`shared_controller_rejected`, WC4 C13.8); two mutex values with distinct
  controllers are both accepted (`distinct_controllers_ok`, WC4 S9);

import Ern.Concurrency.Sync
import Ern.Concurrency.Transfer
import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

/-!
# Reference synchronization library

Library state separate from `S_C` (WC4 C2, C12), on the pattern of `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` (Spec
1 §46, §55, §56):

* the registry of `SyncEntry { guarded, grant }` (WC4 C12), liveness of an entry, the positional
  `ControlOf` relationship (WC4 C12) for declared field positions `MutexLayout`;
* `SyncInv` (WC4 C21.1–C21.7) and `GrantDiscipline` (WC4 C22);
* the library instantiation of `K_C.SyncAuthorized` on the registry (WC4 C14.1–C14.3), and the
  contract obligation `SyncSound` of WC4 C14 ("cannot be used outside the corresponding valid
  synchronization contract");
* derived operations `newMutex` (C13), `acquire` (C16), `unlock` (C17), `resetLock` (C18);
* the arena registry of Spec 1 §46 beside the synchronization registry (WC4 C2, C19), and the
  derived arena operations O17–O19 of `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` (Spec 1 §76–§78, Part XIV) executed
  by a context: `newArena`, `issue` (`split` then `store`, both as executed by the context, WC4
  C2), `reset` (`derive` then `release` on the view of the context); the guard of Spec 1 §56
  (§76.4, WC4 C13.7) of `newArena` and `newMutex` reads both registries;
* labelled library steps, the by-value composite included (WC4 C23), runs, and the encapsulation
  hypothesis `EncapsulatedTrace` (WC4 C22.1–C22.3, C22.5; C23), a predicate on runs, never a
  precondition of a kernel operation.
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Registry (WC4 C12) -/

/-- Synchronization entry (WC4 C12): the protected authority `guarded` and the recorded grant. -/
structure SyncEntry where
  guarded : Nat
  grant : Option Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Synchronization registry (WC4 C12), library state separate from `S_C`. -/
abbrev SyncReg := List SyncEntry

/-- Declared field positions of the reference mutex value (WC4 C12: "at its declared field
position", `guardedField`, `controlField`): the position of the field holding `guarded` and that of the controller, among the
ordered children of the mutex value. -/
structure MutexLayout where
  guardedField : Nat
  controlField : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- An entry is live exactly while `guarded` is active (WC4 C12). -/
def SyncEntry.Live (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) : Prop := s.flat.Active e.guarded

/-- Decidability of liveness of an entry (WC4 C12). -/
instance (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) : Decidable (e.Live s) := by
  unfold SyncEntry.Live; infer_instance

/-- Positional `ControlOf` (WC4 C12): `guarded` is held by the field `h` at position
`guardedField` of the mutex value `m` (the structural parent of `h`); the controller is the child
of `m` at position `controlField`. -/
def ControlOf (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) : Option Nat :=
  match (s.A[e.guarded]?).map (·.holder) with
  | some (Holder.place h) =>
    match parentOf s.P h with
    | some m =>
      if (kids s.P m)[L.guardedField]? = some h then (kids s.P m)[L.controlField]? else none
    | none => none
  | _ => none

/-- The `S3` whose current frame is `f` (WC4 C14: `SyncAuthorized` names the requesting frame;
Spec 1 §43 reads the stack only through its top and membership). -/
def SC.viewAt (s : SC) (f : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s.flat with F := f :: s.frames.filter fun g => decide (g ≠ f) }

/-- WC4 C14.3: the frame `f` has effective and exercisable access to `ControlOf(e)` under the
condition of Spec 1 §68.2: some authority exercisable by `f` in a mode at least `Observe` has a
present effective mode on the controller. -/
def CtrlRight (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) (f : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl => ∃ a ∈ List.range s.A.length,
    (s.viewAt f).ExercisableAt a .observe ∧ effective s.flat a ctl ≠ none) False

/-- Decidability of the controller fact. -/
instance (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) (f : Nat) : Decidable (CtrlRight L s e f) := by
  unfold CtrlRight; infer_instance

/-- The authorization facts of WC4 C14 for an entry: C14.1 (live), C14.2 (`grant = none`), C14.3
(`CtrlRight`). -/
def EntryAuth (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) (f : Nat) : Prop :=
  e.Live s ∧ e.grant = none ∧ CtrlRight L s e f

/-- Decidability of the library authorization of an entry. -/
instance (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (e : SyncEntry) (f : Nat) : Decidable (EntryAuth L s e f) := by
  unfold EntryAuth; infer_instance

/-- Instantiation of `K_C.SyncAuthorized(state, sync_registry, guarded, requesting_frame)` by the
library (WC4 C14, C25): an entry of the registry with the requested `guarded` identity satisfies
the authorization facts C14.1–C14.3. -/
def LibSyncAuthorized (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) (g f : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ e ∈ reg, e.guarded = g ∧ EntryAuth L s e f

/-- Decidability of the library instantiation. -/
instance (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) (g f : Nat) :
    Decidable (LibSyncAuthorized L reg s g f) := by
  unfold LibSyncAuthorized; infer_instance

/-- The contract `K_C` instantiated by the library (WC4 C14, C25), the registry type being
`SyncReg` (WC4 C2). -/
def libKC (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) : KC SyncReg :=
  { k with SyncAuthorized := LibSyncAuthorized L }

/-- Decidability of the instantiated predicate. -/
instance (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) (g f : Nat) :
    Decidable ((libKC k L).SyncAuthorized reg s g f) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (LibSyncAuthorized L reg s g f))

/-- Contract obligation of WC4 C14 ("cannot be used outside the corresponding valid
synchronization contract"), in state `s` with registry `reg`: `SyncAuthorized` holds only for the
`guarded` of a live entry of `reg`. -/
def SyncSound (kc : KC SyncReg) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) : Prop :=
  ∀ g f, kc.SyncAuthorized reg s g f → ∃ e ∈ reg, e.guarded = g ∧ e.Live s

/-- The library instantiation satisfies the obligation of WC4 C14. -/
theorem libKC_sound (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) :
    SyncSound (libKC k L) reg s :=
  fun _ _ ⟨e, he, hg, hl, _⟩ => ⟨e, he, hg, hl⟩

/-- The holder is a usable place (WC4 C12, C13.1, C21.1). -/
def PlaceUsable (t : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .place q => t.Usable q
  | .frame _ => False

/-- Decidability of `PlaceUsable` (WC4 C12). -/
instance (t : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (PlaceUsable t h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold PlaceUsable <;> infer_instance

/-- Spec 1 §65.3 for an authority held by a place `q`: it covers neither a leaf of `q` nor a leaf
of storage transitively owned by `q` (WC4 C13.5). -/
def StoredOK (P : List Place) (y : Authority) : Prop :=
  match y.holder with
  | .place q => ∀ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∉ footprint P q ∧
      ∀ r ∈ List.range P.length, OwnedIn P q r → l ∉ footprint P r
  | .frame _ => True

/-- Decidability of `StoredOK` (Spec 1 §65.3). -/
instance (P : List Place) (y : Authority) : Decidable (StoredOK P y) := by
  unfold StoredOK; split <;> infer_instance

/-- The place `slot` holding `guarded` (WC4 C12). -/
def slotOf (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match (s.A[g]?).map (·.holder) with
  | some (Holder.place h) => some h
  | _ => none

/-! ## Invariants (WC4 C21, C22) -/

/-- Active descendant of `guarded` covering a protected leaf, a leaf of `footprint(guarded)`
(WC4 C13.9, C18.2, C21.5, C22). -/
def CoveringDesc (s : SC) (g j : Nat) : Prop :=
  g ∈ s.flat.ancs j ∧ s.flat.Active j ∧ ∃ l ∈ s.flat.afp j, l ∈ s.flat.afp g

/-- Decidability of `CoveringDesc` (WC4 C22). -/
instance (s : SC) (g j : Nat) : Decidable (CoveringDesc s g j) := by
  unfold CoveringDesc; infer_instance

/-- No active descendant of `guarded` covers a protected leaf (WC4 C13.9, C18.2, C22). -/
def NoCoveringDesc (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Prop := ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ CoveringDesc s g j

/-- Decidability of `NoCoveringDesc` (WC4 C22). -/
instance (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Decidable (NoCoveringDesc s g) := by
  unfold NoCoveringDesc; infer_instance

/-- `GrantDiscipline` (WC4 C22). -/
def GrantDiscipline (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → e.grant = none → NoCoveringDesc s e.guarded

/-- WC4 C21.4, first clause: distinct live entries (by position in the registry) have distinct
`ControlOf` leaves. -/
def CtlUnique (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i j : Nat) (e e' : SyncEntry) (ctl : Nat), reg[i]? = some e → reg[j]? = some e' →
    e.Live s → e'.Live s → ControlOf L s e = some ctl → ControlOf L s e' = some ctl → i = j

/-- WC4 C21.7, initialization invariant for `slot`: for every live entry, every structural leaf of
the place holding `guarded` is `Init`. -/
def SlotInit (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s →
    OptP (slotOf s e.guarded) (fun q => ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.I l = .init) False

/-- WC4 C21.7, initialization invariant for `ctl`: for every live entry, the controller leaf
`ControlOf(entry)` is `Init`. -/
def CtlInit (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl => s.I ctl = .init) False

/-- `SyncInv` (WC4 C21.1–C21.7): items 1–5 and 7 over live entries, item 6 over every entry. -/
structure SyncInv (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C21.1: `guarded` is active (liveness), has own mode `Modify`, and is held by a usable
  place. -/
  guarded : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (s.A[e.guarded]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify ∧
    PlaceUsable s.flat y.holder) False
  /-- WC4 C21.2: a recorded grant exists, has origin `guarded` and footprint
  `footprint(guarded)`. -/
  grant : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → ∀ g, e.grant = some g → OptP (s.A[g]?) (fun y =>
    y.origin = some e.guarded ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ s.flat.afp e.guarded) False
  /-- WC4 C21.3, with the positional `ControlOf` of WC4 C12: the controller exists and is a usable
  leaf. -/
  control : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl =>
    s.flat.Usable ctl ∧ isLeaf s.P ctl) False
  /-- WC4 C21.4, first clause: controller uniqueness among live entries. -/
  ctlUnique : CtlUnique L s reg
  /-- WC4 C21.4, second clause (the guarded-identity uniqueness guard of WC4 C13.7): distinct
  live entries have distinct `guarded` identities. -/
  unique : ∀ (i j : Nat) (e e' : SyncEntry), reg[i]? = some e → reg[j]? = some e' →
    e.Live s → e'.Live s →
    e.guarded = e'.guarded → i = j
  /-- WC4 C21.5, `GrantSubtree`. -/
  grantSubtree : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → ∀ g, e.grant = some g → s.flat.Active g →
    ∀ j, CoveringDesc s e.guarded j → j = g ∨ g ∈ s.flat.ancs j
  /-- WC4 C21.6, `RegBound`, over every entry: the registered `guarded` identity exists (Spec 1
  §38: identities are indices). -/
  regBound : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.guarded < s.A.length
  /-- WC4 C21.7: the structural leaves of `slot` are `Init`. -/
  slotInit : SlotInit s reg
  /-- WC4 C21.7: the controller leaf is `Init`. -/
  ctlInit : CtlInit L s reg

/-! ## Arena registry and the registries of live administrations (Spec 1 §46, §56) -/

/-- The arena registry (Spec 1 §46): library state separate from the kernel state and from the
synchronization registry (WC4 C2: library administration states remain separate from `S_C`). -/
abbrev ArenaReg := List Arena.ArenaEntry

/-- The synchronization registry as a registry of live administrations (Spec 1 §56; WC4 C13.7):
the `guarded` identities of its live entries. -/
def liveGuardeds (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : List Nat :=
  (reg.filter fun e => decide (e.Live s)).map (·.guarded)

/-! ## Derived operations (WC4 C13, C16–C18) -/

/-- The mutex value `M` of WC4 C12, C13: the immediate structural parent of the place `slot`
holding `guarded`. -/
def mutexOf (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match (s.A[g]?).map (·.holder) with
  | some (Holder.place h) => parentOf s.P h
  | _ => none

/-- Preconditions of `newMutex(guarded)` executed by `c` (WC4 C13.1–C13.10), the arena registry
`ar` being the other registry of live administrations (Spec 1 §56). The interface and realization
obligations of WC4 C13 (C13.3, C13.6, initial physical controller state) are not represented: WC4
C13 says they "are not claimed to follow from the authority-only state `S_C`". -/
structure NewMutexPre (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (ar : ArenaReg) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg)
    (c g : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C13.1: `guarded` is active, of own mode `Modify`, and held by a usable place. -/
  guarded : OptP (s.A[g]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
    PlaceUsable s.flat y.holder) False
  /-- WC4 C13.2: ordinary exercisable `Modify` over `guarded` (Spec 1 §43). -/
  exercisable : (s.view c).ExercisableAt g .modify
  /-- WC4 C13.3, with the positional `ControlOf` of WC4 C12: the controller exists and is a
  usable leaf. -/
  control : OptP (ControlOf L s ⟨g, none⟩) (fun ctl => s.flat.Usable ctl ∧ isLeaf s.P ctl) False
  /-- WC4 C13.4: `footprint(guarded) ∩ footprint(M) = ∅`. -/
  disjointM : OptP (mutexOf s g) (fun m => ∀ l ∈ s.flat.afp g, l ∉ footprint s.P m) False

`guarded` of a live entry of `reg`. -/

  ∀ g f, kc.SyncAuthorized reg s g f → ∃ e ∈ reg, e.guarded = g ∧ e.Live s

/-- The library instantiation satisfies the obligation of WC4 C14. -/
theorem libKC_sound (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (reg : SyncReg) (s : SC) :
    SyncSound (libKC k L) reg s :=
  fun _ _ ⟨e, he, hg, hl, _⟩ => ⟨e, he, hg, hl⟩

/-- The holder is a usable place (WC4 C12, C13.1, C21.1). -/
def PlaceUsable (t : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .place q => t.Usable q
  | .frame _ => False

/-- Decidability of `PlaceUsable` (WC4 C12). -/
instance (t : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (PlaceUsable t h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold PlaceUsable <;> infer_instance

/-- Spec 1 §65.3 for an authority held by a place `q`: it covers neither a leaf of `q` nor a leaf
of storage transitively owned by `q` (WC4 C13.5). -/
def StoredOK (P : List Place) (y : Authority) : Prop :=
  match y.holder with
  | .place q => ∀ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∉ footprint P q ∧
      ∀ r ∈ List.range P.length, OwnedIn P q r → l ∉ footprint P r
  | .frame _ => True

/-- Decidability of `StoredOK` (Spec 1 §65.3). -/
instance (P : List Place) (y : Authority) : Decidable (StoredOK P y) := by
  unfold StoredOK; split <;> infer_instance

/-- The place `slot` holding `guarded` (WC4 C12). -/
def slotOf (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match (s.A[g]?).map (·.holder) with
  | some (Holder.place h) => some h
  | _ => none

/-! ## Invariants (WC4 C21, C22) -/

/-- Active descendant of `guarded` covering a protected leaf, a leaf of `footprint(guarded)`
(WC4 C13.9, C18.2, C21.5, C22). -/
def CoveringDesc (s : SC) (g j : Nat) : Prop :=
  g ∈ s.flat.ancs j ∧ s.flat.Active j ∧ ∃ l ∈ s.flat.afp j, l ∈ s.flat.afp g

/-- Decidability of `CoveringDesc` (WC4 C22). -/
instance (s : SC) (g j : Nat) : Decidable (CoveringDesc s g j) := by
  unfold CoveringDesc; infer_instance

/-- No active descendant of `guarded` covers a protected leaf (WC4 C13.9, C18.2, C22). -/
def NoCoveringDesc (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Prop := ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ CoveringDesc s g j

/-- Decidability of `NoCoveringDesc` (WC4 C22). -/
instance (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Decidable (NoCoveringDesc s g) := by
  unfold NoCoveringDesc; infer_instance

/-- `GrantDiscipline` (WC4 C22). -/
def GrantDiscipline (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → e.grant = none → NoCoveringDesc s e.guarded

/-- WC4 C21.4, first clause: distinct live entries (by position in the registry) have distinct
`ControlOf` leaves. -/
def CtlUnique (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i j : Nat) (e e' : SyncEntry) (ctl : Nat), reg[i]? = some e → reg[j]? = some e' →
    e.Live s → e'.Live s → ControlOf L s e = some ctl → ControlOf L s e' = some ctl → i = j

/-- WC4 C21.7, initialization invariant for `slot`: for every live entry, every structural leaf of
the place holding `guarded` is `Init`. -/
def SlotInit (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s →
    OptP (slotOf s e.guarded) (fun q => ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.I l = .init) False

/-- WC4 C21.7, initialization invariant for `ctl`: for every live entry, the controller leaf
`ControlOf(entry)` is `Init`. -/
def CtlInit (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl => s.I ctl = .init) False

/-- `SyncInv` (WC4 C21.1–C21.7): items 1–5 and 7 over live entries, item 6 over every entry. -/
structure SyncInv (L : MutexLayout) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C21.1: `guarded` is active (liveness), has own mode `Modify`, and is held by a usable
  place. -/
  guarded : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (s.A[e.guarded]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify ∧
    PlaceUsable s.flat y.holder) False
  /-- WC4 C21.2: a recorded grant exists, has origin `guarded` and footprint
  `footprint(guarded)`. -/
  grant : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → ∀ g, e.grant = some g → OptP (s.A[g]?) (fun y =>
    y.origin = some e.guarded ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ s.flat.afp e.guarded) False
  /-- WC4 C21.3, with the positional `ControlOf` of WC4 C12: the controller exists and is a usable
  leaf. -/
  control : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → OptP (ControlOf L s e) (fun ctl =>
    s.flat.Usable ctl ∧ isLeaf s.P ctl) False
  /-- WC4 C21.4, first clause: controller uniqueness among live entries. -/
  ctlUnique : CtlUnique L s reg
  /-- WC4 C21.4, second clause (the guarded-identity uniqueness guard of WC4 C13.7): distinct
  live entries have distinct `guarded` identities. -/
  unique : ∀ (i j : Nat) (e e' : SyncEntry), reg[i]? = some e → reg[j]? = some e' →
    e.Live s → e'.Live s →
    e.guarded = e'.guarded → i = j
  /-- WC4 C21.5, `GrantSubtree`. -/
  grantSubtree : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → ∀ g, e.grant = some g → s.flat.Active g →
    ∀ j, CoveringDesc s e.guarded j → j = g ∨ g ∈ s.flat.ancs j
  /-- WC4 C21.6, `RegBound`, over every entry: the registered `guarded` identity exists (Spec 1
  §38: identities are indices). -/
  regBound : ∀ e ∈ reg, e.guarded < s.A.length
  /-- WC4 C21.7: the structural leaves of `slot` are `Init`. -/
  slotInit : SlotInit s reg
  /-- WC4 C21.7: the controller leaf is `Init`. -/
  ctlInit : CtlInit L s reg

/-! ## Arena registry and the registries of live administrations (Spec 1 §46, §56) -/

/-- The arena registry (Spec 1 §46): library state separate from the kernel state and from the
synchronization registry (WC4 C2: library administration states remain separate from `S_C`). -/
abbrev ArenaReg := List Arena.ArenaEntry

/-- The synchronization registry as a registry of live administrations (Spec 1 §56; WC4 C13.7):
the `guarded` identities of its live entries. -/
def liveGuardeds (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) : List Nat :=
  (reg.filter fun e => decide (e.Live s)).map (·.guarded)

/-! ## Derived operations (WC4 C13, C16–C18) -/

/-- The mutex value `M` of WC4 C12, C13: the immediate structural parent of the place `slot`
holding `guarded`. -/
def mutexOf (s : SC) (g : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match (s.A[g]?).map (·.holder) with
  | some (Holder.place h) => parentOf s.P h
  | _ => none

/-- Preconditions of `newMutex(guarded)` executed by `c` (WC4 C13.1–C13.10), the arena registry
`ar` being the other registry of live administrations (Spec 1 §56). The interface and realization
obligations of WC4 C13 (C13.3, C13.6, initial physical controller state) are not represented: WC4
C13 says they "are not claimed to follow from the authority-only state `S_C`". -/
structure NewMutexPre (k : K) (L : MutexLayout) (ar : ArenaReg) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg)
    (c g : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- WC4 C13.1: `guarded` is active, of own mode `Modify`, and held by a usable place. -/
  guarded : OptP (s.A[g]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
    PlaceUsable s.flat y.holder) False
  /-- WC4 C13.2: ordinary exercisable `Modify` over `guarded` (Spec 1 §43). -/
  exercisable : (s.view c).ExercisableAt g .modify
  /-- WC4 C13.3, with the positional `ControlOf` of WC4 C12: the controller exists and is a
  usable leaf. -/
  control : OptP (ControlOf L s ⟨g, none⟩) (fun ctl => s.flat.Usable ctl ∧ isLeaf s.P ctl) False
  /-- WC4 C13.4: `footprint(guarded) ∩ footprint(M) = ∅`. -/
  disjointM : OptP (mutexOf s g) (fun m => ∀ l ∈ s.flat.afp g, l ∉ footprint s.P m) False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (L : MutexLayout) (ar : ArenaReg) (s : SC)
